Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, panicking on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 16
iterations for [ FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-25)Panics

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-108)Examples

```

type Fix = FixedU16<U12>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
```

Overflowing multiply and add.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of `self` × `mul` + `add` and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating

returned.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-117)Examples

```

    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::ONE, Fix::ZERO),
    (Fix::MAX, false)
);

    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::ONE, Fix::DELTA),
    (Fix::MIN, true)
);

    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::from_num(3), Fix::MAX),
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_int(4)
);
```

#### pub const fn [overflowing_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_hypot)(
    self,
    other: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>,
) -> ([FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the hypotenuse and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), indicating whether an
overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 16
iterations for [ FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-123)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U12;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U12>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which wraps to 1
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    (Fix::from_num(1), true)
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

Overflowing inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Computes
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-33)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-125)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four),
    (Fix::from_num(0.5), false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2), true)
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)#### pub const unsafe fn [unchecked_add](https://docs.rs#method.unchecked_add)(self, rhs: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

#### pub const unsafe fn [unchecked_add](https://docs.rs#method.unchecked_add)(self, rhs: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>

Unchecked addition. Computes `self` + `rhs`, assuming
overflow cannot occur.

Calling `x.unchecked_add(y)` is semantically equivalent to
calling
`x.`.[checked_add](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.checked_add)(y).[unwrap_unchecked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.unwrap_unchecked)()

If you’re just trying to avoid the panic in debug mode, then
**do not** use this. Instead, you’re looking for
[ wrapping_add](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.wrapping_add).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

This results in undefined behavior when
`self` + `rhs` > [ MAX](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#associatedconstant.MAX).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedU16%3CFrac%3E-1)

The implementation of items in this block depends on the
number of fractional bits `Frac`.

Creates a fixed-point number from another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-50)Panics

For floating-point numbers, panics if the value is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_from_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.wrapping_from_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-130)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i32), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i64), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f32), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f64), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4-2)));
```
Converts a fixed-point number to another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other type `Dst`for which`FromFixed``Dst::`.[from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)(self)

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-51)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_to_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.wrapping_to_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-131)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I30F2;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(src.to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b111));
// src >> 2 is 0.0111, which for I30F2 is truncated to 0.01
assert_eq!((src >> 2u32).to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b1));
// 2.5 is 10.1 in binary
let two_point_5 = Fix::from_bits(0b101 << (4 - 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i32>(), 2);
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i64>(), 2);
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f32>(), 1.625f32);
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f64>(), 1.625f64);
```

Creates a fixed-point number from another number if it
fits, otherwise returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None).

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[checked_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.checked_to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-132)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(src), Some(Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2))));
let too_large = FixedU16::<U2>::MAX;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_large).is_none());
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(3), Some(Fix::from_bits(3 << 4)));
let too_large = u16::MAX;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_large).is_none());
let too_small = -1;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_small).is_none());
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(1.75f32), Some(expected));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(1.75f64), Some(expected));
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(2e38).is_none());
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(f64::NAN).is_none());
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)#### pub fn [saturating_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-52)Panics

This method panics if the value is a floating-point [NaN](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_nan).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-134)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
let too_large = FixedU16::<U2>::MAX;
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(too_large), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(3), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
let too_small = -1;
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(too_small), Fix::MIN);
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(1.75f32), expected);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(1.75f64), expected);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(2e38), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(f64::NEG_INFINITY), Fix::MIN);
```

For floating-point numbers, panics if the value is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-136)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));

let too_large = FixedU16::<U0>::from_bits(0b1101 << (16 - 7));
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (16 - 4));

// integer 0b1101 << (16 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let large: u16 = 0b1101 << (16 - 7);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (16 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(1.75f32), expected);
// 1.75 << (16 - 4) wraps to binary 11000...
let large = 1.75 * 2f32.powi(16 - 4);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1100 << (16 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
```

// 1.75 << (16 - 4) wraps to binary 11000...

`u16`[or](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.strict_from_num)

`strict_from_num`[instead.](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.from_num)

`from_num`[§](https://docs.rs#planned-deprecation-5)Planned deprecation

This method will be deprecated when the [ strict_from_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.strict_from_num)
method is usable in constant context.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-58)Panics

Panics if the value does not fit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-143)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
const FIVE: Fix = Fix::const_from_int(5);
assert_eq!(FIVE, 5);
```
The following would fail to compile because of overflow.

Parses a fixed-point literal.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

This is similar to [ from_str](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.from_str) but accepts a prefix for setting
the radix, and ignores underscores, such that the parsing is more similar to
numeric literals in Rust code.

Strings starting with “`0b`” are parsed as binary, strings
starting with “`0o`” are parsed as octal, and strings starting with “`0x`” are
parsed as hexadecimal.

Exponents are supported as well. For decimal, binary and octal numbers, the
separator “`e`” or “`E`” can be used to start an exponent, which is then
followed by an optional sign “`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which
is the exponent. For hexadecimal numbers, since “`e`” and “`E`” are hexadecimal
digits, the separator “`@`” has to be used instead. The separator “`@`” is
accepted for all radices. The parsed value is scaled by the radix to the power
of the exponent.

For binary, octal and hexadecimal, base-2 exponents are supported too, using the
separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the
exponent. For example, for hexadecimal “`P8`” means ×2⁸, and is equivalent to
“`@2`” which means ×16².

[§](https://docs.rs#constants)Constants

The `lit` method is useful to write constant fixed-point literals, and can be
evaluated in constant context.

**Warning:** Normal calls to the `lit` method are *not* evaluated at compile
time. To ensure that the call is evaluated at compile time, `lit` must be used
in an inline constant expression, or used to initialize a constant.

For example, here `lit` would be evaluated at compile time:

`const ONE_AND_HALF: Fix = Fix::lit("1.5");`However, here `lit` would be evaluated at run time:

```
// Evaluated at run time.
let one_and_half = Fix::lit("1.5");
```
To evaluate at compile time without introducing a constant into the scope:

`let one_and_half = const { Fix::lit("1.5") };`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-59)Panics

Panics if the number is not valid or overflows.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-144)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("1.75"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("1_.7_5_"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("17.5e-1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0_.017_5_e+0_2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0b1.11"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0b_111e-2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o1.6"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o.16E1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o7p-2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0x1.C"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0x0.1C@1"), 1.75);
```
This method is useful to write constant fixed-point literals.

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
const ONE_AND_HALF: Fix = Fix::lit("1.5");
assert_eq!(ONE_AND_HALF, 1.5);
```
Parses a string slice containing decimal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by 10 to the power of the exponent.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-145)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("1.75"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("0.00625E+3"), Ok(Fix::from_num(6.25)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("1.25e-1"), Ok(Fix::from_num(0.125)));
```

#### pub const fn [from_str_binary](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_binary)(
    src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),

Parses a string slice containing binary digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by the radix (2 for binary) to the power of the exponent.

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The
parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the exponent. For binary, since the
radix is 2, base-2 exponents are equivalent to the other form of exponent.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-146)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.11 in binary is 1.75
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("1.11"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
// 111.0101 in binary is 7.3125
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("1.110101e2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(7.3125)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("11101.01e-2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(7.3125)));
```

Parses a string slice containing octal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by 8 to the power of the exponent.

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-147)Examples

```

```

parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the exponent. For example, for
hexadecimal “`P8`” means ×2⁸, and is equivalent to “`@2`” which means ×16².

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-60)Panics

Panics if the value does not fit or if there is a parsing error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-169)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let f = Fix::strict_from_str("1.75");
assert_eq!(f, Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
```
The following panics because of a parsing error.

Parses an ASCII-byte slice containing octal digits to return a fixed-point number, panicking on overflow.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-66)Panics

Panics if the value does not fit or if there is a parsing error.

```

Parses a string slice containing decimal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the fixed-point number and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating
whether an overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is
returned.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-177)Examples

```

// 9999.5 = 15.5 + 256 × n
assert_eq!(U8F8::overflowing_from_str("9999.5"), Ok((U8F8::from_num(15.5), true)));
```

#### pub const fn [unwrapped_from_ascii_hex](https://docs.rs#method.unwrapped_from_ascii_hex)(src: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)]) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>

renamed to `strict_from_ascii_hex`

Returns the integer part.

Note that for unsigned numbers, this is equivalent to [ floor](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.floor).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-185)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 0010.0000
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
// 0010.0100
let two_and_quarter = two + two / 8;
assert_eq!(two_and_quarter.int(), two);
```
Returns the fractional part.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-186)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
// 0000.0100
let quarter = Fix::ONE / 4;
// 0010.0100
let two_and_quarter = quarter * 9;
assert_eq!(two_and_quarter.frac(), quarter);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)#### pub const fn [round_to_zero](https://docs.rs#method.round_to_zero)(self) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

#### pub const fn [round_to_zero](https://docs.rs#method.round_to_zero)(self) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<Frac>

Rounds to the next integer towards 0.

Note that for unsigned numbers, this is equivalent to [ floor](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.floor).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-187)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.1).round_to_zero(), Fix::from_num(2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.9).round_to_zero(), Fix::from_num(2));
```
Rounds to the next integer towards +∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-78)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the result does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped result can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_ceil](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.wrapping_ceil) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-188)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.5).ceil(), Fix::from_num(3));
```
Rounds to the nearest integer, with ties rounded away from zero.

Returns the square root.

<

[. That is, result ≤ √](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-97)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result overflows.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be returned, but it
is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_lerp](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.wrapping_lerp) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-225)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
let start = Fix::from_num(2);
let end = Fix::from_num(3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.0).lerp(start, end), 2);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.5).lerp(start, end), 2.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.0).lerp(start, end), 3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.0).lerp(start, end), 5);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

Checked multiply and accumulate. Adds (`a` × `b`) to `self`,
or returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow.

Like all other checked methods, this method wraps the successful return value in
an [ Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html). Since the unchecked

[method does not return a value, which is equivalent to returning](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html#method.mul_acc)

`mul_acc`[, this method wraps](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)

`()`[into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)

`()`[Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)([()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html))When overflow occurs, `self` is not modified and retains its previous value.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-231)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
let mut acc = Fix::from_num(3);
let check = acc.checked_mul_acc(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5));
assert_eq!(check, Some(()));
assert_eq!(acc, 5);
acc = Fix::DELTA;
let check = acc.checked_mul_acc(Fix::MAX, Fix::ONE);
assert_eq!(check, None);
// acc is unchanged on error
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::DELTA);
```

#### pub const fn [checked_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.checked_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>>

Checked linear interpolation between `start` and `end`. Returns
[ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow.

The interpolted value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-236)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.5).checked_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), Some(Fix::MAX / 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.5).checked_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), None);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)#### pub const fn [strict_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.strict_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#696-712)

#### pub const fn [strict_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.strict_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [FixedU16](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU16.html)<RangeFrac>

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`, panicking on
overflow.

The interpolated value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-117)Panics

Panics if the result overflows.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-267)Examples

```

use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.5).strict_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), Fix::MAX / 2);
```

Overflowing linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-277)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(0.5).overflowing_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX),
    (Fix::MAX / 2, false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(1.5).overflowing_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_add(Fix::MAX / 2), true)
);
```

```
use fixed::consts;

```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples-279)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U16;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U16>;
assert_eq!(Fix::LN_2, Fix::from_num(consts::LN_2));
assert!(0.5 <= Fix::LN_2 && Fix::LN_2 < 1);
```
These constants are not representable in unsigned fixed-point numbers with less than 1 integer bit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-281)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U15;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U15>;
assert_eq!(Fix::LOG2_E, Fix::from_num(consts::LOG2_E));
assert!(1 <= Fix::LOG2_E && Fix::LOG2_E < 2);
```
The following example fails to compile, since the maximum representable value with 16 fractional bits and 0 integer bits is < 1.

These constants are not representable in unsigned fixed-point numbers with less than 2 integer bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-282)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U14;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U14>;
assert_eq!(Fix::E, Fix::from_num(consts::E));
assert!(2 <= Fix::E && Fix::E < 4);
```
The following example fails to compile, since the maximum representable value with 15 fractional bits and 1 integer bit is < 2.

These constants are not representable in unsigned fixed-point numbers with less than 3 integer bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-283)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U13;
use fixed::FixedU16;
type Fix = FixedU16<U13>;
assert_eq!(Fix::TAU, Fix::from_num(consts::TAU));
assert!(4 <= Fix::TAU && Fix::TAU < 8);
```
The following example fails to compile, since the maximum representable value with 14 fractional bits and 2 integer bits is < 4.

#### fn [from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self

Converts a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-134)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled,
the wrapped value can be returned, but it is not
considered a breaking change if in the future it
panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_from_fixed) instead.

Converts a fixed-pint number.

This conversion never fails (infallible) but may lose precision (lossy). Any fractional bits in the source that cannot be represented in the destination are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_sub-1)

#### fn [overflowing_sub](https://docs.rs/num-traits/0.2.19/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/num_traits/ops/overflowing/trait.OverflowingSub.html#tymethod.overflowing_sub)(&self, v: &Self) -> (Self, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Converts a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-135)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled,
the wrapped value can be returned, but it is not
considered a breaking change if in the future it
panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_to_fixed) instead.

Converts a fixed-point number, panicking if it does not fit.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-136)Panics

Panics if the value does not fit, even when debug assertions are not enabled.

# FixedI32 in fixed - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html

`pub struct FixedI32<Frac> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A 32-bit signed number with `Frac` fractional bits.

The number has 32 bits, of which *f* = `Frac` are
fractional bits and 32 − *f* are integer bits.
The value *x* can lie in the range −231/2 f ≤

*x*< 2

31/2

. The difference between successive numbers is constant throughout the range:

*f**Δ*= 1/2

.

*f*For `FixedI32<`, [U0](https://docs.rs/types/extra/type.U0.html)>*f* = 0 and
*Δ* = 1, and the fixed-point number behaves like an [ i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html) with the value lying in the range −2

31≤

*x*< 2

31. For

`FixedI32<`[U32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/type.U32.html)>,
*f*= 32 and

*Δ*= 1/2

32, and the value lies in the range −1/2 ≤

*x*< 1/2.

`Frac` is an [ Unsigned](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.Unsigned.html) as provided by the

[.](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate`FixedI32<Frac>` has the same size, alignment and ABI as
[ i32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html); it is

`#[repr(transparent)]` with
[as the only non-zero-sized field.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

`i32`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U3;
use fixed::FixedI32;
let eleven = FixedI32::<U3>::from_num(11);
assert_eq!(eleven, FixedI32::<U3>::from_bits(11 << 3));
assert_eq!(eleven, 11);
assert_eq!(eleven.to_string(), "11");
let two_point_75 = eleven / 4;
assert_eq!(two_point_75, FixedI32::<U3>::from_bits(11 << 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_75, 2.75);
assert_eq!(two_point_75.to_string(), "2.8");
```

### impl<Frac> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

The implementation of items in this block is independent
of the number of fractional bits `Frac`.

The difference between any two successive representable numbers, *Δ*.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits, then
*Δ* = 1/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::DELTA, Fix::from_bits(1));
// binary 0.0001 is decimal 0.0625
assert_eq!(Fix::DELTA, 0.0625);
```
The smallest value that can be represented.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits,
then the minimum is −231/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MIN, Fix::from_bits(i32::MIN));
```
The largest value that can be represented.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits, then the maximum is
(231 − 1)/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_bits(i32::MAX));
```
Creates a fixed-point number that has a bitwise representation identical to the given integer.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 0010.0000 = 2
assert_eq!(Fix::from_bits(0b10_0000), 2);
```
Creates an integer that has a bitwise representation identical to the given fixed-point number.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 2 is 0010.0000
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).to_bits(), 0b10_0000);
```
Converts a fixed-point number from big endian to the target’s endianness.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
let f = Fix::from_bits(0x1234_5678);
if cfg!(target_endian = "big") {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_be(f), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_be(f), f.swap_bytes());
}
```
Converts a fixed-point number from little endian to the target’s endianness.

    assert_eq!(Fix::from_le(f), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_le(f), f.swap_bytes());
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [signed_bits](https://docs.rs#method.signed_bits)(self) -> [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

#### pub const fn [signed_bits](https://docs.rs#method.signed_bits)(self) -> [u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html)

Returns the number of bits required to represent the value.

The number of bits required includes an initial one for negative numbers, and an initial zero for non-negative numbers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-26)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-3).signed_bits(), 7);      // “_101.0000”
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-1).signed_bits(), 5);      // “___1.0000”
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-0.0625).signed_bits(), 1); // “____.___1”
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0).signed_bits(), 1);       // “____.___0”
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.0625).signed_bits(), 2);  // “____.__01”
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1).signed_bits(), 6);       // “__01.0000”
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).signed_bits(), 7);       // “_011.0000”
```

Multiplies two fixed-point numbers and returns a wider type to retain all precision.

If `self` has *f* fractional bits and 32 − *f*
integer bits, and `rhs` has *g* fractional bits and 32 − *g* integer bits, then the returned fixed-point number will
have *f* + *g* fractional bits and 64 − *f* − *g* integer bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-33)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::FixedI32;
// decimal: 1.25 × 1.0625 = 1.328_125
// binary: 1.01 × 1.0001 = 1.010101
let a = FixedI32::<U2>::from_num(1.25);
let b = FixedI32::<U4>::from_num(1.0625);
assert_eq!(a.wide_mul(b), 1.328_125);
```

Divides two fixed-point numbers and returns a wider type to retain more precision.

If `self` has *f* fractional bits
and 32 − *f* integer bits, and `rhs` has
*g* fractional bits and 32 − *g* integer
bits, then the returned fixed-point number will
have 32 + *f* − *g* fractional
bits and 32 − *f* + *g* integer
bits.

**Warning:** While most cases of overflow are avoided using this method,
dividing [ MIN](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.MIN) by

`-`[DELTA](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA) will still
result in panic due to overflow. The alternative [method avoids this by sacrificing one fractional bit in the return type.](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wide_sdiv)

`wide_sdiv`[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if the divisor is zero or on overflow. Overflow can only occur when dividing
[ MIN](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.MIN) by

`-`[DELTA](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA).[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U3, U5, U30};
use fixed::{FixedI32, FixedI64};
// decimal: 4.625 / 0.03125 = 148
// binary: 100.101 / 0.00001 = 10010100
let a = FixedI32::<U3>::from_num(4.625);
let b = FixedI32::<U5>::from_num(0.03125);
let ans: FixedI64<U30> = a.wide_div(b);
assert_eq!(ans, 148);
```
The following panics because of overflow.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

Divides two fixed-point numbers and returns a wider type to retain more precision.

If `self` has *f* fractional bits and
32 − *f*
integer bits, and `rhs` has *g* fractional bits and
32 − *g*
integer bits, then the returned fixed-point number will have
31 + *f* − *g*
fractional bits and
33 − *f* + *g*
integer bits.

This is similar to the [ wide_div](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wide_div) method but
sacrifices one fractional bit to avoid overflow.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-1)Panics

Panics if the divisor is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U4, U5, U30};

// binary: 100.101 / 0.00001 = 10010100

let b = FixedI32::<U5>::from_num(0.03125);

```
Unlike [ wide_div](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wide_div), dividing

[by](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.MIN)

`MIN``-`[DELTA](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA) does not overflow.```
use fixed::types::extra::{U4, U31};
use fixed::{FixedI32, FixedI64};
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
type DFix = FixedI64<U31>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MIN.wide_sdiv(-Fix::DELTA), (DFix::MIN / 2).abs());
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

Multiply and add. Returns `self` × `mul` + `add`.

For some cases, the product `self` × `mul` would overflow
on its own, but the final result `self` × `mul` + `add` is representable; in
these cases this method returns the correct result without overflow.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result
overflows. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value
can be returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the
future it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_mul_add](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wrapping_mul_add)
instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-38)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(4).mul_add(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::from_num(3)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.mul_add(Fix::from_num(1.5), -Fix::MAX), Fix::MAX / 2);
```

Returns the mean of `self` and `other`.

This method rounds the result down towards −∞. This is different from the
standard library [ midpoint](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html#method.midpoint), which rounds
towards 0. Rounding down preserves translation invariance, that is

`(a + t).mean(b + t)` = `a.mean(b) + t`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-46)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).mean(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(3.5));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-3).mean(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(0.5));
```
Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 32
iterations for [ FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-6)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result overflows.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be returned, but it
is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wrapping_hypot) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-47)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U28;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U28>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).hypot(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(5));
```

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-8)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

When debug assertions are enabled, this method also panics if the result
overflows. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics;
if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wrapping_inv_lerp) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-49)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
let start = Fix::from_num(2);
let end = Fix::from_num(3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), -1);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 0);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.75).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 0.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3.5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 1);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 2);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

Checked multiply and add.
Returns `self` × `mul` + `add`, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow.

For some cases, the product `self` × `mul` would overflow
on its own, but the final result `self` × `mul` + `add` is representable; in
these cases this method returns the correct result without overflow.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-60)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(4).checked_mul_add(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::from_num(3)),
    Some(Fix::from_num(5))
);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.checked_mul_add(Fix::ONE, Fix::ZERO), Some(Fix::MAX));
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.checked_mul_add(Fix::ONE, Fix::DELTA), None);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.checked_mul_add(Fix::from_num(1.5), -Fix::MAX), Some(Fix::MAX / 2));
```

    self,
    other: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,

#### pub const fn [checked_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.checked_hypot)(
    self,
    other: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, returning [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 32
iterations for [ FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-68)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U28;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U28>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).checked_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Some(Fix::from_num(5))
);
// hypot(2, 7.875) == 8.125, which does not fit
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(2).checked_hypot(Fix::from_num(7.875)),
    None
);
```

Checked inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.
Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow or when

`start` = `end`.The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.checked_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)), None);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [saturating_mul_add](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_mul_add)<MulFrac: [LeEqU32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU32.html)>(
    self,
    mul: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<MulFrac>,
    add: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

#### pub const fn [saturating_mul_add](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_mul_add)<MulFrac: [LeEqU32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU32.html)>(
    self,
    mul: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<MulFrac>,
    add: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

Saturating multiply and add.
Returns `self` × `mul` + `add`, saturating on overflow.

For some cases, the product `self` × `mul` would overflow
on its own, but the final result `self` × `mul` + `add` is representable; in
these cases this method returns the correct result without overflow.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-76)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(4).saturating_mul_add(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::from_num(3)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
let half_max = Fix::MAX / 2;
assert_eq!(half_max.saturating_mul_add(Fix::from_num(3), half_max), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(half_max.saturating_mul_add(Fix::from_num(-5), half_max), Fix::MIN);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_mul_add(Fix::from_num(1.5), -Fix::MAX), half_max);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [saturating_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_hypot)(self, other: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

#### pub const fn [saturating_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_hypot)(self, other: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, saturating on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 32
iterations for [ FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-81)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U28;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U28>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).saturating_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// hypot(2, 7.875) == 8.125, which does not fit
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(2).saturating_hypot(Fix::from_num(7.875)),
    Fix::MAX
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [saturating_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_inv_lerp)<RetFrac: [LeEqU32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU32.html)>(

    self,

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
saturating on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-13)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-83)Examples

```

use fixed::FixedI32;

let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four), 0.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::ZERO), Fix::MIN);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_hypot)(self, other: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

#### pub const fn [wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_hypot)(self, other: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, wrapping on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 32
iterations for [ FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-96)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U28;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U28>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).wrapping_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// hypot(2, 7.875) == 8.125, which wraps to -7.875
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(2).wrapping_hypot(Fix::from_num(7.875)),
    Fix::from_num(-7.875)
);
```

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
wrapping on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-16)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-98)Examples

```

use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).wrapping_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four), 0.5);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.wrapping_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2)
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [strict_mul_add](https://docs.rs#method.strict_mul_add)<MulFrac: [LeEqU32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU32.html)>(
    self,
    mul: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<MulFrac>,
    add: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

#### pub const fn [strict_mul_add](https://docs.rs#method.strict_mul_add)<MulFrac: [LeEqU32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU32.html)>(
    self,
    mul: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<MulFrac>,
    add: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

Strict multiply and add.
Returns `self` × `mul` + `add`, panicking on overflow.

For some cases, the product `self` × `mul` would overflow
on its own, but the final result `self` × `mul` + `add` is representable; in
these cases this method returns the correct result without overflow.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-21)Panics

Panics if the result does not fit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-105)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(4).strict_mul_add(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::from_num(3)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.strict_mul_add(Fix::from_num(1.5), -Fix::MAX), Fix::MAX / 2);
```
The following panics because of overflow.

#### pub const fn [strict_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.strict_inv_lerp)<RetFrac: [LeEqU32](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU32.html)>(
    self,
    start: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
    end: [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<RetFrac>

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
panicking on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-30)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end` or when the results overflows.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-115)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).strict_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four), 0.5);
```
The following panics because `start` = `end`.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```

use fixed::FixedI32;

```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

Overflowing multiply and add.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of `self` × `mul` + `add` and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating
whether an overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is
returned.

For some cases, the product `self` × `mul` would overflow
on its own, but the final result `self` × `mul` + `add` is representable; in
these cases this method returns the correct result without overflow.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-121)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::ONE, Fix::ZERO),
    (Fix::MAX, false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::ONE, Fix::DELTA),
    (Fix::MIN, true)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::from_num(3), Fix::MAX),
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_int(4)
);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_mul_add(Fix::from_num(1.5), -Fix::MAX),
    (Fix::MAX / 2, false)
);
```

#### pub const fn [overflowing_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_hypot)(

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the hypotenuse and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), indicating whether an
overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 32
iterations for [ FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-128)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U28;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U28>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
// hypot(2, 7.875) == 8.125, which wraps to -7.875
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(2).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(7.875)),
    (Fix::from_num(-7.875), true)
);
```

Overflowing inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Computes
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-35)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-130)Examples

```

use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four),
    (Fix::from_num(0.5), false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2), true)
);
```

Overflowing addition with an unsigned fixed-point number.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the sum and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating
whether an overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped
value is returned.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-131)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::{FixedI32, FixedU32};
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
type UFix = FixedU32<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(-5).overflowing_add_unsigned(UFix::from_num(3)),
    (Fix::from_num(-2), false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::ZERO.overflowing_add_unsigned(UFix::MAX),
    (-Fix::DELTA, true)
);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedI32%3CFrac%3E-1)

The implementation of items in this block depends on the
number of fractional bits `Frac`.

Creates a fixed-point number from another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-52)Panics

For floating-point numbers, panics if the value is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_from_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wrapping_from_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-135)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i32), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-3i64), Fix::from_bits(-3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f32), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-1.75f64), Fix::from_bits(-0b111 << (4-2)));
```
Converts a fixed-point number to another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other type `Dst`for which`FromFixed``Dst::`.[from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)(self)

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-53)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_to_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.wrapping_to_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-136)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I30F2;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(src.to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b111));
// src >> 2 is 0.0111, which for I30F2 is truncated to 0.01
assert_eq!((src >> 2u32).to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b1));
// 2.5 is 10.1 in binary
let two_point_5 = Fix::from_bits(0b101 << (4 - 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i32>(), 2);
assert_eq!((-two_point_5).to_num::<i64>(), -3);
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f32>(), 1.625f32);
assert_eq!((-one_point_625).to_num::<f64>(), -1.625f64);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub fn [checked_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.checked_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)

#### pub fn [checked_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.checked_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>>

Creates a fixed-point number from another number if it
fits, otherwise returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None).

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[checked_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.checked_to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-137)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(src), Some(Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2))));
let too_large = FixedI32::<U2>::MAX;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_large).is_none());
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(3), Some(Fix::from_bits(3 << 4)));
let too_large = i32::MAX;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_large).is_none());
let too_small = i32::MIN;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_small).is_none());
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(1.75f32), Some(expected));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(-1.75f64), Some(-expected));
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(2e38).is_none());
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(f64::NAN).is_none());
```

fits, otherwise returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None).

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`

- Any other type `Dst`for which`FromFixed``Dst::`.[checked_from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.checked_from_fixed)(self)

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-138)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4, U6};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
let expected = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));

assert_eq!((-two_point_5).checked_to_num::<i64>(), Some(-3));
type AllInt = FixedI32<U0>;
assert!(AllInt::from_bits(-1).checked_to_num::<u32>().is_none());
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-139)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};

assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(-1.75f64), -expected);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(2e38), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(f64::NEG_INFINITY), Fix::MIN);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-141)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
// integer 0b1101 << (32 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let too_large = FixedI32::<U0>::from_bits(0b1101 << (32 - 7));
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (32 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(too_large), wrapped);
// integer 0b1101 << (32 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let large: i32 = 0b1101 << (32 - 7);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (32 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(1.75f32), expected);
// 1.75 << (32 - 4) wraps to binary 11000...
let large = 1.75 * 2f32.powi(32 - 4);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1100 << (32 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
```

type TooFewIntBits = FixedI32<U6>;
let wrapped = TooFewIntBits::from_bits(Fix::MAX.to_bits() << 2);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.overflowing_to_num::<TooFewIntBits>(), (wrapped, true));
// 2.5 is 10.1 in binary
let two_point_5 = Fix::from_bits(0b101 << (4 - 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_5.overflowing_to_num::<i32>(), (2, false));
let does_not_fit = FixedI32::<U0>::from_bits(-1);
let wrapped = 1u32.wrapping_neg();
assert_eq!(does_not_fit.overflowing_to_num::<u32>(), (wrapped, true));
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.overflowing_to_num::<f32>(), (1.625f32, false));
```

Parses a fixed-point literal.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

This is similar to [ from_str](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_str) but accepts a prefix for setting
the radix, and ignores underscores, such that the parsing is more similar to
numeric literals in Rust code.

The string can start with “`-`” for a negative number.

Strings starting with “`0b`” are parsed as binary, strings
starting with “`0o`” are parsed as octal, and strings starting with “`0x`” are
parsed as hexadecimal.

Exponents are supported as well. For decimal, binary and octal numbers, the
separator “`e`” or “`E`” can be used to start an exponent, which is then
followed by an optional sign “`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which
is the exponent. For hexadecimal numbers, since “`e`” and “`E`” are hexadecimal
digits, the separator “`@`” has to be used instead. The separator “`@`” is
accepted for all radices. The parsed value is scaled by the radix to the power
of the exponent.

For binary, octal and hexadecimal, base-2 exponents are supported too, using the
separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the
exponent. For example, for hexadecimal “`P8`” means ×2⁸, and is equivalent to
“`@2`” which means ×16².

[§](https://docs.rs#constants)Constants

The `lit` method is useful to write constant fixed-point literals, and can be
evaluated in constant context.

**Warning:** Normal calls to the `lit` method are *not* evaluated at compile
time. To ensure that the call is evaluated at compile time, `lit` must be used
in an inline constant expression, or used to initialize a constant.

For example, here `lit` would be evaluated at compile time:

`const ONE_AND_HALF: Fix = Fix::lit("1.5");`However, here `lit` would be evaluated at run time:

```
// Evaluated at run time.
let one_and_half = Fix::lit("1.5");
```
To evaluate at compile time without introducing a constant into the scope:

`let one_and_half = const { Fix::lit("1.5") };`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-61)Panics

Panics if the number is not valid or overflows.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-149)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("1.75"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("1_.7_5_"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("17.5e-1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0_.017_5_e+0_2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("-01.75"), -1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0b1.11"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0b_111e-2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("-0b1.11"), -1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o1.6"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o.16E1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o7p-2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0x1.C"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0x0.1C@1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("-0x1.C"), -1.75);
```
This method is useful to write constant fixed-point literals.

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
const ONE_AND_HALF: Fix = Fix::lit("1.5");
assert_eq!(ONE_AND_HALF, 1.5);
```
Parses a string slice containing decimal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by 10 to the power of the exponent.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-150)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("1.75"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("-1.75"), Ok(Fix::from_num(-1.75)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("0.00625E+3"), Ok(Fix::from_num(6.25)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("1.25e-1"), Ok(Fix::from_num(0.125)));
```

#### pub const fn [from_str_binary](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_binary)(

Parses a string slice containing binary digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by the radix (2 for binary) to the power of the exponent.

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The
parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the exponent. For binary, since the
radix is 2, base-2 exponents are equivalent to the other form of exponent.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-151)Examples

```

use fixed::FixedI32;

assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("-1.11"), Ok(Fix::from_num(-1.75)));
// 111.0101 in binary is 7.3125
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("1.110101e2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(7.3125)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("11101.01e-2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(7.3125)));
```

Parses a string slice containing octal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-152)Examples

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#806-822)#### pub const fn [strict_from_str](https://docs.rs#method.strict_from_str)(src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

#### pub const fn [strict_from_str](https://docs.rs#method.strict_from_str)(src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [FixedI32](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI32.html)<Frac>

Parses a string slice containing decimal digits to return a fixed-point number, panicking on overflow.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-62)Panics

Panics if the value does not fit or if there is a parsing error.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-174)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI32;
type Fix = FixedI32<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let f = Fix::strict_from_str("1.75");
assert_eq!(f, Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
```
The following panics because of a parsing error.
