#### pub const fn [saturating_mul_acc](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_mul_acc)<AFrac: [LeEqU128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU128.html), BFrac: [LeEqU128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU128.html)>(
    &mut self,
    a: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<AFrac>,
    b: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<BFrac>,
)

Saturating multiply and accumulate. Adds (`a` × `b`) to `self`,
saturating on overflow.

For some cases, the product `a` × `b` would overflow on its
own, but the final result `self` + `a` × `b` is representable; in these cases
this method saves the correct result without overflow.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-246)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
let mut acc = Fix::from_num(3);
acc.saturating_mul_acc(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5));
assert_eq!(acc, 5);
acc = Fix::MAX / 2;
acc.saturating_mul_acc(Fix::MAX / 2, Fix::from_num(3));
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::MAX);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
acc = -Fix::MAX;
acc.saturating_mul_acc(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(1.5));
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::MAX / 2);
```

#### pub const fn [saturating_sqrt](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_sqrt)(self) -> Self

Returns the square root, saturating on overflow.

This method uses an iterative method, with up to 128 iterations for
[ FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html). The result is rounded down, and the error is
<

[. That is, result ≤ √](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self` < result + `DELTA`.Overflow can only occur when there are no integer bits and
the representable range is −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5.
In this case, the method returns [ MAX](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html#associatedconstant.MAX) for an input value ≥ 0.25.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-106)Panics

Panics if the number is negative.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-248)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U4, U128};
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).saturating_sqrt(), Fix::SQRT_2);

assert_eq!(AllFrac::from_num(0.25).saturating_sqrt(), AllFrac::MAX);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)#### pub const fn [saturating_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,

    end: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,

#### pub const fn [saturating_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_lerp)<RangeFrac>(

    end: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`, saturating on
overflow.

The interpolated value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

```

assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.5).saturating_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-2.0).saturating_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), Fix::MIN);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3.0).saturating_lerp(Fix::MAX, Fix::ZERO), Fix::MIN);
```

#### pub const fn [wrapping_signum](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_signum)(self) -> [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<Frac>

Wrapping signum. Returns a number representing
the sign of `self`, wrapping on overflow.

Overflow can only occur

- if the value is positive and the fixed-point number has zero or one integer bits such that it cannot hold the value 1.
- if the value is negative and the fixed-point number has zero integer bits, such that it cannot hold the value −1.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-250)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U4, U127, U128};
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(5).wrapping_signum(), 1);
assert_eq!(Fix::ZERO.wrapping_signum(), 0);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-5).wrapping_signum(), -1);
type OneIntBit = FixedI128<U127>;
type ZeroIntBits = FixedI128<U128>;
assert_eq!(OneIntBit::from_num(0.5).wrapping_signum(), -1);
assert_eq!(ZeroIntBits::from_num(0.25).wrapping_signum(), 0);
assert_eq!(ZeroIntBits::from_num(-0.5).wrapping_signum(), 0);
```

#### pub const fn [strict_signum](https://docs.rs#method.strict_signum)(self) -> [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<Frac>

Strict signum. Returns a number representing
the sign of `self`, panicking on overflow.

Overflow can only occur

- if the value is positive and the fixed-point number has zero or one integer bits such that it cannot hold the value 1.
- if the value is negative and the fixed-point number has zero integer bits, such that it cannot hold the value −1.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

Adds `self` to the product `a` × `b`, panicking on overflow.

For some cases, the product `a` × `b` would
overflow on its own, but the final result `self` + `a` × `b`
is representable; in these cases this method returns the correct result without
overflow.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-118)Panics

Panics if the result does not fit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-266)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).strict_add_prod(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    5
);
// -MAX + MAX × 1.5 = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(
    (-Fix::MAX).strict_add_prod(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(1.5)),
    Fix::MAX / 2
);
```
The following panics because of overflow.

#### pub const fn [strict_mul_acc](https://docs.rs#method.strict_mul_acc)<AFrac: [LeEqU128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU128.html), BFrac: [LeEqU128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU128.html)>(
    &mut self,
    a: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<AFrac>,
    b: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<BFrac>,
)

Strict multiply and accumulate. Adds (`a` × `b`) to `self`,
panicking on overflow.

For some cases, the product `a` × `b` would overflow on its
own, but the final result `self` + `a` × `b` is representable; in these cases
this method saves the correct result without overflow.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-119)Panics

Panics if the result does not fit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-267)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
let mut acc = Fix::from_num(3);
acc.strict_mul_acc(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5));
assert_eq!(acc, 5);
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
acc = -Fix::MAX;
acc.strict_mul_acc(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(1.5));
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::MAX / 2);
```

#### pub const fn [strict_sqrt](https://docs.rs#method.strict_sqrt)(self) -> Self

Returns the square root, panicking for negative numbers and on overflow.

This method uses an iterative method, with up to 128 iterations for
[ FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html). The result is rounded down, and the error is
<

[. That is, result ≤ √](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self` < result + `DELTA`.Overflow can only occur when there are no integer bits and
the representable range is −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5.
In this case, the method panics for an input value ≥ 0.25.

    end: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

#### pub const fn [strict_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.strict_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`, panicking on
overflow.

The interpolated value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

For some cases, the product `a` × `b` would
overflow on its own, but the final result `self` + `a` × `b`
is representable; in these cases this method returns the correct result without
overflow.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-279)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_add_prod(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_add_prod(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(3)),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(4), true)
);
// -MAX + MAX × 1.5 = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
assert_eq!(
    (-Fix::MAX).overflowing_add_prod(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(1.5)),
    (Fix::MAX / 2, false)
);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

Overflowing multiply and accumulate. Adds (`a` × `b`) to `self`,
wrapping and returning [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if overflow occurs.

For some cases, the product `a` × `b` would overflow on its
own, but the final result `self` + `a` × `b` is representable; in these cases
this method saves the correct result without overflow.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-280)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
let mut acc = Fix::from_num(3);
assert!(!acc.overflowing_mul_acc(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5)));
assert_eq!(acc, 5);
acc = Fix::MAX;
assert!(acc.overflowing_mul_acc(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(3)));
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(4));
// MAX × 1.5 - MAX = MAX / 2, which does not overflow
acc = -Fix::MAX;
assert!(!acc.overflowing_mul_acc(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_num(1.5)));
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::MAX / 2);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)#### pub const fn [overflowing_rem_euclid_int](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_rem_euclid_int)(
    self,
    rhs: [i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html),
) -> ([FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<Frac>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

#### pub const fn [overflowing_rem_euclid_int](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_rem_euclid_int)(
    self,
    rhs: [i128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i128.html),
) -> ([FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<Frac>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Remainder for Euclidean division by an integer.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the remainder and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating whether an overflow has
occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

Note that while remainder for Euclidean division cannot be negative, the wrapped value can be negative.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-129)Panics

Panics if the divisor is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-281)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U124;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U124>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(7.5).overflowing_rem_euclid_int(2), (Fix::from_num(1.5), false));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-7.5).overflowing_rem_euclid_int(2), (Fix::from_num(0.5), false));
// -8 ≤ Fix < 8, so the answer 12.5 wraps to -3.5
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(-7.5).overflowing_rem_euclid_int(20), (Fix::from_num(-3.5), true));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)#### pub const fn [overflowing_sqrt](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_sqrt)(self) -> (Self, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

#### pub const fn [overflowing_sqrt](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_sqrt)(self) -> (Self, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Returns the square root.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow has occurred. On
overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

This method uses an iterative method, with up to 128 iterations for
[ FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html). The result is rounded down, and the error is
<

[. That is, result ≤ √](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self` < result + `DELTA`.Overflow can only occur when there are no integer bits and
the representable range is −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5.
In this case, overflow occurs for an input value ≥ 0.25.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-130)Panics

Panics if the number is negative.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-282)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U4, U128};
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(2).overflowing_sqrt(),
    (Fix::SQRT_2, false)
);
type AllFrac = FixedI128<U128>;
assert_eq!(
    AllFrac::from_num(0.25).overflowing_sqrt(),
    (AllFrac::from_num(-0.5), true)
);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)#### pub const fn [overflowing_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> ([FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#843-864)

#### pub const fn [overflowing_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> ([FixedI128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI128.html)<RangeFrac>, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Overflowing linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The interpolated value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-283)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedI128;
type Fix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(0.5).overflowing_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX),
    (Fix::MAX / 2, false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(1.5).overflowing_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_add(Fix::MAX / 2), true)
);
```

#### fn [from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self

Converts a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-143)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled,
the wrapped value can be returned, but it is not
considered a breaking change if in the future it
panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_from_fixed) instead.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/traits.rs.html#5524)

[§](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_from_fixed)

Converts a fixed-point number, saturating if it does not fit.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

Converts a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-144)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled,
the wrapped value can be returned, but it is not
considered a breaking change if in the future it
panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_to_fixed) instead.

# FixedU128 in fixed - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/struct.FixedU128.html

`pub struct FixedU128<Frac> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A 128-bit unsigned number with `Frac` fractional bits.

The number has 128 bits, of which *f* = `Frac` are
fractional bits and 128 − *f* are integer bits.
The value *x* can lie in the range 0 ≤ *x* < 2128/2 f. The difference between successive
numbers is constant throughout the range:

*Δ*= 1/2

.

*f*For `FixedU128<`, [U0](https://docs.rs/types/extra/type.U0.html)>*f* = 0 and
*Δ* = 1, and the fixed-point number behaves like a [ u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html) with the value lying in the range 0 ≤

*x*< 2

128. For

`FixedU128<`[U128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/type.U128.html)>,
*f*= 128 and

*Δ*= 1/2

128, and the value lies in the range 0 ≤

*x*< 1.

`Frac` is an [ Unsigned](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.Unsigned.html) as provided by the

[.](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate`FixedU128<Frac>` has the same size, alignment and ABI as
[ u128](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html); it is

`#[repr(transparent)]` with
[as the only non-zero-sized field.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html)

`u128`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U3;
use fixed::FixedU128;
let eleven = FixedU128::<U3>::from_num(11);
assert_eq!(eleven, FixedU128::<U3>::from_bits(11 << 3));
assert_eq!(eleven, 11);
assert_eq!(eleven.to_string(), "11");
let two_point_75 = eleven / 4;
assert_eq!(two_point_75, FixedU128::<U3>::from_bits(11 << 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_75, 2.75);
assert_eq!(two_point_75.to_string(), "2.8");
```

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedU128%3CFrac%3E)

### impl<Frac> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

The implementation of items in this block is independent
of the number of fractional bits `Frac`.

The difference between any two successive representable numbers, *Δ*.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits, then
*Δ* = 1/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::DELTA, Fix::from_bits(1));
// binary 0.0001 is decimal 0.0625
assert_eq!(Fix::DELTA, 0.0625);
```
The smallest value that can be represented.

The minimum of unsigned numbers is 0.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MIN, Fix::from_bits(u128::MIN));
```
The largest value that can be represented.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits, then the maximum is
(2128 − 1)/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_bits(u128::MAX));
```
Creates a fixed-point number that has a bitwise representation identical to the given integer.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 0010.0000 = 2
assert_eq!(Fix::from_bits(0b10_0000), 2);
```
Creates an integer that has a bitwise representation identical to the given fixed-point number.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 2 is 0010.0000
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).to_bits(), 0b10_0000);
```
Converts a fixed-point number from big endian to the target’s endianness.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let f = Fix::from_bits(0x1234_5678_9ABC_DEF0_0102_0304_0506_0708);
if cfg!(target_endian = "big") {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_be(f), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_be(f), f.swap_bytes());
}
```
Converts a fixed-point number from little endian to the target’s endianness.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

    assert_eq!(Fix::from_le(f), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_le(f), f.swap_bytes());
}
```

Returns the distance from `self` to `other`.

The distance is the absolute value of the difference.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;

```
Returns the mean of `self` and `other`.

This method rounds the result down towards −∞. This is different from the
standard library [ midpoint](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u128.html#method.midpoint), which rounds
towards 0. Rounding down preserves translation invariance, that is

`(a + t).mean(b + t)` = `a.mean(b) + t`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).mean(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(3.5));
```
Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 128
iterations for [ FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result overflows.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be returned, but it
is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_hypot) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-38)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U124;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U124>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).hypot(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(5));
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

When debug assertions are enabled, this method also panics if the result
overflows. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics;
if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_inv_lerp) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-40)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let start = Fix::from_num(2);
let end = Fix::from_num(3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 0);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.75).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 0.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3.5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 1);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 2);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-7)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the
result overflows. When debug assertions are not enabled, the
wrapped value can be returned, but it is not considered a
breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_sub_signed](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_sub_signed) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-44)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::{FixedI128, FixedU128};
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
type IFix = FixedI128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(5).sub_signed(IFix::from_num(-3)), 8);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [checked_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.checked_hypot)(
    self,
    other: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

#### pub const fn [checked_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.checked_hypot)(
    self,
    other: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, returning [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 128
iterations for [ FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-60)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U124;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U124>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).checked_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Some(Fix::from_num(5))
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which does not fit
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).checked_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    None
);
```

Checked inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.
Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow or when

`start` = `end`.The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-62)Examples

assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).checked_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, two), None);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.checked_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)), None);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [saturating_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

#### pub const fn [saturating_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, saturating on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 128
iterations for [ FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-73)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U124;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U124>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).saturating_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which does not fit
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).saturating_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    Fix::MAX
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [saturating_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_inv_lerp)<RetFrac: [LeEqU128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU128.html)>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>,

#### pub const fn [saturating_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_inv_lerp)<RetFrac: [LeEqU128](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU128.html)>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>,
    end: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RetFrac>

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
saturating on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-10)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-75)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four), 0.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::ZERO), Fix::MIN);
```

);
```

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
wrapping on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-13)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-89)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).wrapping_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four), 0.5);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.wrapping_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2)
);
```

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, panicking on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 128
iterations for [ FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-23)Panics

Panics if the result does not fit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-104)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U124;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U124>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
```

assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(5).strict_sub_signed(IFix::from_num(-3)), 8);
```

Overflowing multiply and add.

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the hypotenuse and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), indicating whether an
overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 128
iterations for [ FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-119)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U124;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U124>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which wraps to 1
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    (Fix::from_num(1), true)
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

Overflowing inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Computes
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-31)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-121)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four),
    (Fix::from_num(0.5), false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2), true)
);
```

Calling `x.unchecked_add(y)` is semantically equivalent to
calling
`x.`.[checked_add](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.checked_add)(y).[unwrap_unchecked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.unwrap_unchecked)()

**do not** use this. Instead, you’re looking for
[ wrapping_add](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_add).

This results in undefined behavior when
`self` + `rhs` > [ MAX](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.MAX).

Unchecked multiplication by an integer. Computes
`self` × `rhs`, assuming overflow cannot occur.

Calling `x.unchecked_mul_int(y)` is semantically equivalent to
calling
`x.`.[checked_mul_int](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.checked_mul_int)(y).[unwrap_unchecked](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#method.unwrap_unchecked)()

If you’re just trying to avoid the panic in debug mode, then
**do not** use this. Instead, you’re looking for
[ wrapping_mul_int](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_mul_int).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-4)Safety

This results in undefined behavior when
`self` × `rhs` > [ MAX](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.MAX).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedU128%3CFrac%3E-1)

The implementation of items in this block depends on the
number of fractional bits `Frac`.

Creates a fixed-point number from another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-48)Panics

For floating-point numbers, panics if the value is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_from_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_from_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-126)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i32), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i64), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f32), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f64), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4-2)));
```
Converts a fixed-point number to another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other type `Dst`for which`FromFixed``Dst::`.[from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)(self)

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-49)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_to_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_to_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-127)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I30F2;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(src.to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b111));
// src >> 2 is 0.0111, which for I30F2 is truncated to 0.01
assert_eq!((src >> 2u32).to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b1));
// 2.5 is 10.1 in binary
let two_point_5 = Fix::from_bits(0b101 << (4 - 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i32>(), 2);
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i64>(), 2);
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f32>(), 1.625f32);
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f64>(), 1.625f64);
```

#### pub fn [checked_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.checked_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>>

Creates a fixed-point number from another number if it
fits, otherwise returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None).

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[checked_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.checked_to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-128)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(src), Some(Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2))));
let too_large = FixedU128::<U2>::MAX;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_large).is_none());
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(3), Some(Fix::from_bits(3 << 4)));
let too_large = u128::MAX;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_large).is_none());
let too_small = -1;
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(too_small).is_none());
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(1.75f32), Some(expected));
assert_eq!(Fix::checked_from_num(1.75f64), Some(expected));
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(2e38).is_none());
assert!(Fix::checked_from_num(f64::NAN).is_none());
```

The other number can be:

- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4, U6};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary

assert_eq!(two_point_5.checked_to_num::<i64>(), Some(2));
type AllInt = FixedU128<U0>;
assert!(AllInt::MAX.checked_to_num::<i128>().is_none());
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.checked_to_num::<f32>(), Some(1.625f32));

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub fn [saturating_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

#### pub fn [saturating_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

Creates a fixed-point number from another number, saturating if it does not fit.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[saturating_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.saturating_to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-50)Panics

This method panics if the value is a floating-point [NaN](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_nan).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-130)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
let too_large = FixedU128::<U2>::MAX;
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(too_large), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(3), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
let too_small = -1;
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(too_small), Fix::MIN);
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(1.75f32), expected);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(1.75f64), expected);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(2e38), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::saturating_from_num(f64::NEG_INFINITY), Fix::MIN);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-132)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4};

use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));

// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(1.75f32), expected);
// 1.75 << (128 - 4) wraps to binary 11000...
let large = 1.75 * 2f32.powi(128 - 4);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1100 << (128 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
```

The following would fail to compile because of overflow.

Parses a fixed-point literal.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

This is similar to [ from_str](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.from_str) but accepts a prefix for setting
the radix, and ignores underscores, such that the parsing is more similar to
numeric literals in Rust code.

Strings starting with “`0b`” are parsed as binary, strings
starting with “`0o`” are parsed as octal, and strings starting with “`0x`” are
parsed as hexadecimal.

Exponents are supported as well. For decimal, binary and octal numbers, the
separator “`e`” or “`E`” can be used to start an exponent, which is then
followed by an optional sign “`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which
is the exponent. For hexadecimal numbers, since “`e`” and “`E`” are hexadecimal
digits, the separator “`@`” has to be used instead. The separator “`@`” is
accepted for all radices. The parsed value is scaled by the radix to the power
of the exponent.

For binary, octal and hexadecimal, base-2 exponents are supported too, using the
separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the
exponent. For example, for hexadecimal “`P8`” means ×2⁸, and is equivalent to
“`@2`” which means ×16².

[§](https://docs.rs#constants)Constants

The `lit` method is useful to write constant fixed-point literals, and can be
evaluated in constant context.

**Warning:** Normal calls to the `lit` method are *not* evaluated at compile
time. To ensure that the call is evaluated at compile time, `lit` must be used
in an inline constant expression, or used to initialize a constant.

For example, here `lit` would be evaluated at compile time:

`const ONE_AND_HALF: Fix = Fix::lit("1.5");`However, here `lit` would be evaluated at run time:

```
// Evaluated at run time.
let one_and_half = Fix::lit("1.5");
```
To evaluate at compile time without introducing a constant into the scope:

`let one_and_half = const { Fix::lit("1.5") };`[§](https://docs.rs#panics-57)Panics

Panics if the number is not valid or overflows.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-140)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("1.75"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("1_.7_5_"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("17.5e-1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0_.017_5_e+0_2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0b1.11"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0b_111e-2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o1.6"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o.16E1"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0o7p-2"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0x1.C"), 1.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::lit("0x0.1C@1"), 1.75);
```
This method is useful to write constant fixed-point literals.

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
const ONE_AND_HALF: Fix = Fix::lit("1.5");
assert_eq!(ONE_AND_HALF, 1.5);
```
Parses a string slice containing decimal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by 10 to the power of the exponent.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-141)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("1.75"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("0.00625E+3"), Ok(Fix::from_num(6.25)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str("1.25e-1"), Ok(Fix::from_num(0.125)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [from_str_binary](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_binary)(

#### pub const fn [from_str_binary](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_binary)(
    src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>, [ParseFixedError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseFixedError.html)>

Parses a string slice containing binary digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by the radix (2 for binary) to the power of the exponent.

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The
parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the exponent. For binary, since the
radix is 2, base-2 exponents are equivalent to the other form of exponent.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-142)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.11 in binary is 1.75
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("1.11"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
// 111.0101 in binary is 7.3125
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("1.110101e2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(7.3125)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_binary("11101.01e-2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(7.3125)));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [from_str_octal](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_octal)(

#### pub const fn [from_str_octal](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_octal)(

Parses a string slice containing octal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. The separator “`e`”, “`E`” or “`@`”
can be used to start an exponent, which is then followed by an optional sign
“`+`” or “`-`”, and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed
value is scaled by 8 to the power of the exponent.

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The
parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the exponent. For example, for octal
“`P6`” means ×2⁶, and is equivalent to “`E2`” which means ×8².

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-143)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary, 1.6 in octal
let f = Fix::from_str_octal("1.6");
let check = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(f, Ok(check));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_octal("160e-2"), Ok(check));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [from_str_hex](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_hex)(src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>, [ParseFixedError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseFixedError.html)>

#### pub const fn [from_str_hex](https://docs.rs#method.from_str_hex)(src: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>, [ParseFixedError](https://docs.rs/struct.ParseFixedError.html)>

Parses a string slice containing hexadecimal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

The number can have an optional exponent. Since “`e`” and “`E`” are valid
hexadecimal digits, they cannot be used as a separator to start an exponent, so
“`@`” is used instead. This is then followed by an optional sign “`+`” or “`-`”,
and then by a decimal integer which is the exponent. The parsed value is scaled
by 16 to the power of the exponent.

Base-2 exponents are supported too, using the separator “`p`” or “`P`”. The
parsed value is scaled by 2 to the power of the exponent. For example, for
hexadecimal “`P8`” means ×2⁸, and is equivalent to “`@2`” which means ×16².

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-144)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.C in hexadecimal is 1.75
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_hex("1.C"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_hex("1C@-1"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_str_hex(".01C@+2"), Ok(Fix::from_num(1.75)));
```

type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary, 1.C in hexadecimal
let f = Fix::strict_from_ascii_hex(b"1.C");
assert_eq!(f, Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
```
The following panics because of a parsing error.

Parses a string slice containing decimal digits to return a fixed-point number.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the fixed-point number and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating

returned.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-173)Examples

```

// 9999.5 = 15.5 + 256 × n
assert_eq!(U8F8::overflowing_from_str("9999.5"), Ok((U8F8::from_num(15.5), true)));
```

Returns the integer part.

Note that for unsigned numbers, this is equivalent to [ floor](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.floor).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-181)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 0010.0000
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
// 0010.0100
let two_and_quarter = two + two / 8;
assert_eq!(two_and_quarter.int(), two);
```
Returns the fractional part.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-182)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
// 0000.0100
let quarter = Fix::ONE / 4;
// 0010.0100
let two_and_quarter = quarter * 9;
assert_eq!(two_and_quarter.frac(), quarter);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [round_to_zero](https://docs.rs#method.round_to_zero)(self) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

#### pub const fn [round_to_zero](https://docs.rs#method.round_to_zero)(self) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<Frac>

Rounds to the next integer towards 0.

Note that for unsigned numbers, this is equivalent to [ floor](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.floor).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-183)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.1).round_to_zero(), Fix::from_num(2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.9).round_to_zero(), Fix::from_num(2));
```
Rounds to the next integer towards +∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-76)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the result does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped result can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_ceil](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_ceil) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-184)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.5).ceil(), Fix::from_num(3));
```
Rounds to the nearest integer, with ties rounded away from zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-77)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the result does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped result can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_round](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_round) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-186)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.5).round(), Fix::from_num(3));
```

Returns the square root.

<

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-95)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result overflows.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be returned, but it
is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_lerp](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.wrapping_lerp) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-221)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let start = Fix::from_num(2);
let end = Fix::from_num(3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.0).lerp(start, end), 2);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.5).lerp(start, end), 2.75);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.0).lerp(start, end), 3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.0).lerp(start, end), 5);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

Checked multiply and accumulate. Adds (`a` × `b`) to `self`,
or returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) on overflow.

Like all other checked methods, this method wraps the successful return value in
an [ Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html). Since the unchecked

[method does not return a value, which is equivalent to returning](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#method.mul_acc)

`mul_acc`[, this method wraps](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)

`()`[into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html)

`()`[Some](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.Some)([()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html))When overflow occurs, `self` is not modified and retains its previous value.

The `a` and `b` parameters can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-227)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
let mut acc = Fix::from_num(3);
let check = acc.checked_mul_acc(Fix::from_num(4), Fix::from_num(0.5));
assert_eq!(check, Some(()));
assert_eq!(acc, 5);
acc = Fix::DELTA;
let check = acc.checked_mul_acc(Fix::MAX, Fix::ONE);
assert_eq!(check, None);
// acc is unchanged on error
assert_eq!(acc, Fix::DELTA);
```

#### pub const fn [saturating_sqrt](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_sqrt)(self) -> Self

Returns the square root, saturating on overflow. Can never overflow for unsigned numbers.

This method uses an iterative method, with up to 128 iterations for
[ FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html). The result is rounded down, and the error is
<

[. That is, result ≤ √](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self` < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-241)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).saturating_sqrt(), Fix::SQRT_2);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [saturating_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)

#### pub const fn [saturating_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`, saturating on
overflow.

The interpolated value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-242)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(0.5).saturating_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), Fix::MAX / 2);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.5).saturating_lerp(Fix::ZERO, Fix::MAX), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3.0).saturating_lerp(Fix::MAX, Fix::ZERO), Fix::ZERO);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#750-771)#### pub const fn [strict_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.strict_lerp)<RangeFrac>(

    end: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,

#### pub const fn [strict_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.strict_lerp)<RangeFrac>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,
    end: [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>,
) -> [FixedU128](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU128.html)<RangeFrac>

Linear interpolation between `start` and `end`, panicking on
overflow.

The interpolated value is
`start` + `self` × (`end` − `start`). This
is `start` when `self` = 0, `end` when `self` = 1, and
linear interpolation for all other values of `self`. Linear extrapolation is
performed if `self` is not in the range 0 ≤ *x* ≤ 1.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-274)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U128;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U128>;
assert_eq!(Fix::LOG10_2, Fix::from_num(consts::LOG10_2));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#examples-275)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U128;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U128>;
assert_eq!(Fix::LN_2, Fix::from_num(consts::LN_2));
assert!(0.5 <= Fix::LN_2 && Fix::LN_2 < 1);
```
These constants are not representable in unsigned fixed-point numbers with less than 1 integer bit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-277)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U127;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U127>;
assert_eq!(Fix::LOG2_E, Fix::from_num(consts::LOG2_E));
assert!(1 <= Fix::LOG2_E && Fix::LOG2_E < 2);
```
The following example fails to compile, since the maximum representable value with 128 fractional bits and 0 integer bits is < 1.

These constants are not representable in unsigned fixed-point numbers with less than 2 integer bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-278)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U126;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U126>;
assert_eq!(Fix::E, Fix::from_num(consts::E));
assert!(2 <= Fix::E && Fix::E < 4);
```
The following example fails to compile, since the maximum representable value with 127 fractional bits and 1 integer bit is < 2.

These constants are not representable in unsigned fixed-point numbers with less than 3 integer bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-279)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::extra::U125;
use fixed::FixedU128;
type Fix = FixedU128<U125>;
assert_eq!(Fix::TAU, Fix::from_num(consts::TAU));
assert!(4 <= Fix::TAU && Fix::TAU < 8);
```
The following example fails to compile, since the maximum representable value with 126 fractional bits and 2 integer bits is < 4.

#### fn [from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self

Converts a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-132)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled,
the wrapped value can be returned, but it is not
considered a breaking change if in the future it
panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_from_fixed) instead.

#### fn [overflowing_sub](https://docs.rs/num-traits/0.2.19/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/num_traits/ops/overflowing/trait.OverflowingSub.html#tymethod.overflowing_sub)(&self, v: &Self) -> (Self, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Converts a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-133)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled,
the wrapped value can be returned, but it is not
considered a breaking change if in the future it
panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_to_fixed) instead.

# LossyFrom in fixed::traits - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/traits/trait.LossyFrom.html

```
pub trait LossyFrom<Src> {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[lossy_from](https://docs.rs#tymethod.lossy_from)(src: Src) -> Self;
}## Expand description

This trait provides infallible conversions that might be lossy.

This trait is implemented for conversions between integer primitives, floating-point primitives and fixed-point numbers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::traits::LossyFrom;
use fixed::types::{I12F4, I8F24};
// original is 0x12.345678, lossy is 0x012.3
let original = I8F24::from_bits(0x1234_5678);
let lossy = I12F4::lossy_from(original);
assert_eq!(lossy, I12F4::from_bits(0x0123));
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# LossyInto in fixed::traits - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/traits/trait.LossyInto.html

```
pub trait LossyInto<Dst> {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[lossy_into](https://docs.rs#tymethod.lossy_into)(self) -> Dst;
}## Expand description

This trait provides infallible conversions that might be lossy.
This is the reciprocal of [ LossyFrom](https://docs.rs/trait.LossyFrom.html).

Usually [ LossyFrom](https://docs.rs/trait.LossyFrom.html) should be implemented instead of this trait;
there is a blanket implementation which provides this trait when

[is implemented (similar to](https://docs.rs/trait.LossyFrom.html)

`LossyFrom`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::traits::LossyInto;
use fixed::types::{I12F4, I8F24};
// original is 0x12.345678, lossy is 0x012.3
let original = I8F24::from_bits(0x1234_5678);
let lossy: I12F4 = original.lossy_into();
assert_eq!(lossy, I12F4::from_bits(0x0123));
```

# LosslessTryFrom in fixed::traits - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/traits/trait.LosslessTryFrom.html

`pub trait LosslessTryFrom<Src>: `[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required method
    fn [lossless_try_from](https://docs.rs#tymethod.lossless_try_from)(src: Src) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self>;
}## Expand description

This trait provides lossless conversions that might be fallible.

This trait is implemented for conversions between integer primitives, floating-point primitives and fixed-point numbers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::traits::LosslessTryFrom;
use fixed::types::{I24F8, I4F12};
// original is 0x000001.23, lossless is 0x1.230
let original = I24F8::from_bits(0x0000_0123);
let lossless = I4F12::lossless_try_from(original);
assert_eq!(lossless, Some(I4F12::from_bits(0x1230)));
// too_large is 0x000012.34, 0x12.340 does not fit in I4F12
let too_large = I24F8::from_bits(0x0000_1234);
let overflow = I4F12::lossless_try_from(too_large);
assert_eq!(overflow, None);
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

# LosslessTryInto in fixed::traits - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/traits/trait.LosslessTryInto.html

```
pub trait LosslessTryInto<Dst> {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[lossless_try_into](https://docs.rs#tymethod.lossless_try_into)(self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Dst>;
}## Expand description

This trait provides lossless conversions that might be fallible.
This is the reciprocal of [ LosslessTryFrom](https://docs.rs/trait.LosslessTryFrom.html).

Usually [ LosslessTryFrom](https://docs.rs/trait.LosslessTryFrom.html) should be implemented instead of this
trait; there is a blanket implementation which provides this trait
when

[is implemented (similar to](https://docs.rs/trait.LosslessTryFrom.html)

`LosslessTryFrom`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into`[).](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::traits::LosslessTryInto;
use fixed::types::{I24F8, I4F12};
// original is 0x000001.23, lossless is 0x1.230
let original = I24F8::from_bits(0x0000_0123);
let lossless: Option<I4F12> = original.lossless_try_into();
assert_eq!(lossless, Some(I4F12::from_bits(0x1230)));
// too_large is 0x000012.34, 0x12.340 does not fit in I4F12
let too_large = I24F8::from_bits(0x0000_1234);
let overflow: Option<I4F12> = too_large.lossless_try_into();
assert_eq!(overflow, None);
```

       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html);

[wrapping_from_fixed](https://docs.rs#tymethod.wrapping_from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self;
[overflowing_from_fixed](https://docs.rs#tymethod.overflowing_from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> (Self, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html);
    // Provided methods
    fn [strict_from_fixed](https://docs.rs#method.strict_from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) { ... }
[unwrapped_from_fixed](https://docs.rs#method.unwrapped_from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self
       where Self: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) { ... }
}## Expand description

This trait provides checked conversions from fixed-point numbers.

This trait is implemented for conversions between integer primitives, floating-point primitives and fixed-point numbers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::traits::FromFixed;
use fixed::types::U8F8;
// 0x87.65
let f = U8F8::from_bits(0x8765);
assert_eq!(f32::from_fixed(f), f32::from(0x8765u16) / 256.0);
assert_eq!(i32::checked_from_fixed(f), Some(0x87));
assert_eq!(u8::saturating_from_fixed(f), 0x87);
// no fit
assert_eq!(i8::checked_from_fixed(f), None);
assert_eq!(i8::saturating_from_fixed(f), i8::MAX);
assert_eq!(i8::wrapping_from_fixed(f), 0x87u8 as i8);
assert_eq!(i8::overflowing_from_fixed(f), (0x87u8 as i8, true));
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/traits.rs.html#4631)

#### fn [from_fixed](https://docs.rs#tymethod.from_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(src: F) -> Self

Converts from a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does
not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped
value can be returned, but it is not considered a breaking
change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is required use
[ wrapping_from_fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_from_fixed) instead.

}## Expand description

This trait provides checked conversions to fixed-point numbers.

This trait is implemented for conversions between integer primitives, floating-point primitives and fixed-point numbers.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::traits::ToFixed;
use fixed::types::{U8F8, U16F16};
let f: U8F8 = 13.5f32.to_fixed();
assert_eq!(f, U8F8::from_bits((13 << 8) | (1 << 7)));
// 0x1234.5678 is too large and can be wrapped to 0x34.56
let too_large = U16F16::from_bits(0x1234_5678);
let checked: Option<U8F8> = too_large.checked_to_num();
assert_eq!(checked, None);
let saturating: U8F8 = too_large.saturating_to_num();
assert_eq!(saturating, U8F8::MAX);
let wrapping: U8F8 = too_large.wrapping_to_num();
assert_eq!(wrapping, U8F8::from_bits(0x3456));
let overflowing: (U8F8, bool) = too_large.overflowing_to_num();
assert_eq!(overflowing, (U8F8::from_bits(0x3456), true));
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Converts to a fixed-point number.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if `self` is a floating-point number that is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

When debug assertions are enabled, also panics if the value
does not fit. When debug assertions are not enabled, the
wrapped value can be returned, but it is not considered a
breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_to_fixed) instead.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/traits.rs.html#4784)#### fn [overflowing_to_fixed](https://docs.rs#tymethod.overflowing_to_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(self) -> (F, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/traits.rs.html#4784)

#### fn [overflowing_to_fixed](https://docs.rs#tymethod.overflowing_to_fixed)<F: [Fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.Fixed.html)>(self) -> (F, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Converts to a fixed-point number.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the fixed-point number and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)
indicating whether an overflow has occurred. On overflow, the
wrapped value is returned.

Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

Panics if `self` is a floating-point number that is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

Converts an integer to a fixed-point number, wrapping if it does not fit.

Converts a floating-point number to a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-42)Panics

Panics if `self` is not [finite](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html#method.is_finite).

When debug assertions are enabled, also panics if the value does not
fit. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_to_fixed](https://docs.rs/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.wrapping_to_fixed) instead.

Converts a floating-point number to a fixed-point number.

Rounding is to the nearest, with ties rounded to even.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-47)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, also panics if the value does not

# fixed::consts - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/consts/index.html

## Expand description

Mathematical constants.

The constants have the maximum precision possible for a fixed-point number, and are rounded down at that precision.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::consts;
use fixed::types::I4F28;
let tau = I4F28::from_num(consts::TAU);
println!("τ = 2π with eight binary places is {tau:.8b}");
assert_eq!(format!("{tau:.8b}"), "110.01001000");
println!("τ = 2π with eight decimal places is {tau:.8}");
assert_eq!(format!("{tau:.8}"), "6.28318531");
```

# fixed::f128 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/f128/index.html

## Expand description

Constants specific to the [ F128](https://docs.rs/struct.F128.html) quadruple-precision floating-point type.

Mathematically significant numbers are provided in the [ consts](https://docs.rs/consts/index.html) sub-module.

For constants related to the floating-point representation itself, see the
associated constants defined directly on the [ F128](https://docs.rs/struct.F128.html) type.

[§](https://docs.rs#planned-deprecation)Planned deprecation

This module will be deprecated when the [ f128 feature](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/116909) is ready and
stabilized.

- [consts](https://docs.rs/consts/index.html)
- Basic mathematical constants.

# F128 in fixed - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/1.31.0/fixed/struct.F128.html

`pub struct F128 { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A *binary128* floating-point number (`f128`).

This type can be used to

- convert between fixed-point numbers and the bit representation of 128-bit floating-point numbers.
- compare fixed-point numbers and the bit representation of 128-bit floating-point numbers.

This type does *not* support arithmetic or general analytic functions.

Please see [ Quadruple-precision floating-point format on
Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruple-precision_floating-point_format) for more information on

*binary128*.

*See also the *

[fixed](https://docs.rs/index.html)::

[f128](https://docs.rs/f128/index.html)::

[consts](https://docs.rs/f128/consts/index.html)module.

[§](https://docs.rs#planned-deprecation)Planned deprecation

This struct will be deprecated when the [ f128 feature](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/116909) is ready and
stabilized.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::F128;
assert_eq!(I16F16::ONE.to_num::<F128>(), F128::ONE);
assert_eq!(I16F16::from_num(F128::ONE), I16F16::ONE);
// fixed-point numbers can be compared directly to F128 values
assert!(I16F16::from_num(1.5) > F128::ONE);
assert!(I16F16::from_num(0.5) < F128::ONE);
```
