# fixed 1.6.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/1.6.0

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers.

- `FixedI8`- `FixedU8`
- `FixedI16`- `FixedU16`
- `FixedI32`- `FixedU32`
- `FixedI64`- `FixedU64`
- `FixedI128`- `FixedU128`

These types can have `Frac` fractional bits, where
0 ≤ `Frac` ≤ n and n is the total number of bits. When
`Frac` = 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an n-bit
integer. When `Frac` = n, the value x lies in the range
−0.5 ≤ x < 0.5 for signed numbers, and in the range
0 ≤ x < 1 for unsigned numbers.

In version 1 the [ typenum crate](https://crates.io/crates/typenum) is used for the fractional bit
count

`Frac`; the plan is to to have a major version 2 with [const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)instead when the Rust compiler support for them is powerful enough.

The main features are

- Representation of fixed-point numbers up to 128 bits wide.
- Conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Comparisons between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Parsing from strings in decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Display as decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Arithmetic and logic operations.

This crate does *not* provide general analytic functions.

- No algebraic functions are provided, for example no `sqrt`or`pow`.
- No trigonometric functions are provided, for example no `sin`or`cos`.
- No other transcendental functions are provided, for example no
`log`or`exp`.

These functions are not provided because different implementations can have different trade-offs, for example trading some correctness for speed. Implementations can be provided in other crates.

- The *fixed-sqrt*crate

The conversions supported cover the following cases.

- Infallible lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using `From``Into`
- Infallible lossy conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LosslessTryFrom``LosslessTryInto`
- Checked conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric
primitives are provided using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`[their checked versions](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.checked_from_num).
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

## What’s new

### Version 1.6.0 news (2021-02-05)

- The crate now requires rustc version 1.47.0 or later.
- The optional *az*crate[version 1.1](https://docs.rs/az/~1.1/az/index.html).
- The `unsigned_abs``FixedSigned`
- The following methods are now `const`functions:
- The `unwrapped_to_fixed``ToFixed`
- The `unwrapped_from_fixed``FromFixed`

Details on other releases can be found in [ RELEASES.md](https://gitlab.com/tspiteri/fixed/blob/master/RELEASES.md).

## Quick examples

```
use I20F12;
// 19/3 = 6 1/3

// four decimal digits for 12 binary digits
assert_eq!;
// find the ceil and convert to i32
assert_eq!;
// we can also compare directly to integers
assert_eq!;
```
The type [ I20F12](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/type.I20F12.html) is a 32-bit fixed-point signed number with 20
integer bits and 12 fractional bits. It is an alias to

[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html)<

[U12](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/extra/type.U12.html)>. The unsigned counterpart would be

[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````

// multiplication and division by integers are possible

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (~0.0002)
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_num;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (~3.4)

assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (~3.2). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (~3.4).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.6/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.4/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````
use ;
// −8 ≤ I4F4 < 8 with steps of 1/16 (~0.06)
let a = I4F4from_num;
// multiplication and division by integers are possible
let ans1 = a / 5 * 17;
// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (~3.2)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (~0.0002)
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_num;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (~3.4)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (~3.2). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (~3.4).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.4/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.4/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.4/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.4/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.4/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

`from_num`## Writing fixed-point constants and values literally

The [ fixed-macro crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed-macro) provides a convenient macro to write down
fixed-point constants literally in the code.

```
use I16F16;
use fixed;
const NUM1: I16F16 = fixed!;
let num2 = NUM1 + fixed!;
assert_eq!;
```
## Using the *fixed* crate

The *fixed* crate is available on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fixed). To use
it in your crate, add it as a dependency inside [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "1.4"
```
The *fixed* crate requires rustc version 1.44.0 or later.

## Optional features

The *fixed* crate has four optional feature:

- `az`, disabled by default. This implements the cast traits provided by the- *az*crate
- `f16`, disabled by default. This provides conversion to/from- `f16`- `bf16`- *half*crate
- `serde`, disabled by default. This provides serialization support for the fixed-point types. This feature requires the- *serde*crate
- `std`, disabled by default. This is for features that are not possible under- `no_std`: currently the implementation of the- `Error`- `ParseFixedError`

To enable features, you can add the dependency like this to
[ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "1.4"
 = ["f16", "serde"]
```
## Experimental optional features

It is not considered a breaking change if experimental features are removed. The removal of experimental features would however require a minor version bump. Similarly, on a minor version bump, optional dependencies can be updated to an incompatible newer version.

There are three experimental feature:

- `num-traits`, disabled by default. This implements some traits from the- *num-traits*crate- *num-traits*reaches version 1.0.0.)
- `unwrapped`, disabled by default. This adds methods for arithmetic that panic on overflow even when debug assertions are disabled, similar to how wrapping methods will wrap even when debug assertions are enabled. (The plan is to always enable this functionality but remove the experimental feature in version 1.5.0.)
- `serde-str`, disabled by default. Fixed-point numbers are serialized as strings showing the value when using human-readable formats. This feature requires the- `serde`and the- `std`optional features. (The plan is to upgrade this to an optional feature in version 1.5.0.)- **Warning:**numbers serialized when this feature is enabled cannot be deserialized when this feature is disabled, and vice versa.

# fixed 1.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/1.3.0

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers.

- `FixedI8`- `FixedU8`
- `FixedI16`- `FixedU16`
- `FixedI32`- `FixedU32`
- `FixedI64`- `FixedU64`
- `FixedI128`- `FixedU128`

These types can have `Frac` fractional bits, where
0 ≤ `Frac` ≤ n and n is the total number of bits. When
`Frac` = 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an n-bit
integer. When `Frac` = n, the value x lies in the range
−0.5 ≤ x < 0.5 for signed numbers, and in the range
0 ≤ x < 1 for unsigned numbers.

In version 1 the [ typenum crate](https://crates.io/crates/typenum) is used for the fractional bit
count

`Frac`; the plan is to to have a major version 2 with [const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are supported by the Rust compiler.

The main features are

- Representation of fixed-point numbers up to 128 bits wide.
- Conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Comparisons between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Parsing from strings in decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Display as decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Arithmetic and logic operations.

This crate does *not* provide general analytic functions.

- No algebraic functions are provided, for example no `sqrt`or`pow`.
- No trigonometric functions are provided, for example no `sin`or`cos`.
- No other transcendental functions are provided, for example no
`log`or`exp`.

These functions are not provided because different implementations can have different trade-offs, for example trading some correctness for speed. Implementations can be provided in other crates.

- The *fixed-sqrt*crate

The conversions supported cover the following cases.

- Infallible lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using `From``Into`
- Infallible lossy conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LosslessTryFrom``LosslessTryInto`
- Checked conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric
primitives are provided using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`[their checked versions](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.3/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.checked_from_num).
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (~3.2). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (~3.4).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.1/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.1/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.1/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.1/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.1/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

`from_num`## Using the *fixed* crate

The *fixed* crate is available on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fixed). To use
it in your crate, add it as a dependency inside [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "1.1"
```
The *fixed* crate requires rustc version 1.44.0 or later.

## Optional features

The *fixed* crate has four optional feature:

- `az`, disabled by default. This implements the cast traits provided by the- *az*crate
- `f16`, disabled by default. This provides conversion to/from- `f16`- `bf16`- *half*crate
- `serde`, disabled by default. This provides serialization support for the fixed-point types. This feature requires the- *serde*crate
- `std`, disabled by default. This is for features that are not possible under- `no_std`: currently the implementation of the- `Error`- `ParseFixedError`

To enable features, you can add the dependency like this to
[ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "1.1"
 = ["f16", "serde"]
```
## Experimental optional features

It is not considered a breaking change if experimental features are removed. The removal of experimental features would however require a minor version bump. Similarly, on a minor version bump, optional dependencies can be updated to an incompatible newer version.

There is one experimental feature:

- `num-traits`, disabled by default. This implements some traits from the- *num-traits*crate

# fixed 1.0.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/1.0.0

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers.

- `FixedI8`- `FixedU8`
- `FixedI16`- `FixedU16`
- `FixedI32`- `FixedU32`
- `FixedI64`- `FixedU64`
- `FixedI128`- `FixedU128`

These types can have `Frac` fractional bits, where
0 ≤ `Frac` ≤ n and n is the total number of bits. When
`Frac` = 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an n-bit
integer. When `Frac` = n, the value x lies in the range
−0.5 ≤ x < 0.5 for signed numbers, and in the range
0 ≤ x < 1 for unsigned numbers.

In version 1 the [ typenum crate](https://crates.io/crates/typenum) is used for the fractional bit
count

`Frac`; the plan is to to have a major version 2 with [const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are supported by the Rust compiler.

The main features are

- Representation of fixed-point numbers up to 128 bits wide.
- Conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Comparisons between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Parsing from strings in decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Display as decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Arithmetic and logic operations.

This crate does *not* provide general analytic functions.

- No algebraic functions are provided, for example no `sqrt`or`pow`.
- No trigonometric functions are provided, for example no `sin`or`cos`.
- No other transcendental functions are provided, for example no
`log`or`exp`.

These functions are not provided because different implementations can have different trade-offs, for example trading some correctness for speed. Implementations can be provided in other crates.

- The *fixed-sqrt*crate

The conversions supported cover the following cases.

- Infallible lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using `From``Into`
- Infallible lossy conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LosslessTryFrom``LosslessTryInto`
- Checked conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric
primitives are provided using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`[their checked versions](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.checked_from_num).
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

## Quick examples

```
use I20F12;
// 19/3 = 6 1/3
let six_and_third = I20F12from_num / 3;
// four decimal digits for 12 binary digits
assert_eq!;
// find the ceil and convert to i32
assert_eq!;
// we can also compare directly to integers
assert_eq!;
```
The type [ I20F12](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/type.I20F12.html) is a 32-bit fixed-point signed number with 20
integer bits and 12 fractional bits. It is an alias to

[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html)<

[U12](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/extra/type.U12.html)>. The unsigned counterpart would be

[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````
use ;
// −8 ≤ I4F4 < 8 with steps of 1/16 (~0.06)
let a = I4F4from_num;
// multiplication and division by integers are possible
let ans1 = a / 5 * 17;
// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (~3.2)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (~0.0002)
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_num;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (~3.4)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (~3.2). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (~3.4).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.0/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers.

- `FixedI8`- `FixedU8`
- `FixedI16`- `FixedU16`
- `FixedI32`- `FixedU32`
- `FixedI64`- `FixedU64`
- `FixedI128`- `FixedU128`

These types can have `Frac` fractional bits, where
0 ≤ `Frac` ≤ n and n is the total number of bits. When
`Frac` = 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an n-bit
integer. When `Frac` = n, the value x lies in the range
−0.5 ≤ x < 0.5 for signed numbers, and in the range
0 ≤ x < 1 for unsigned numbers.

Currently the [ typenum crate](https://crates.io/crates/typenum) is used for the fractional bit count

`Frac`; it is planned to move to [const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are supported by the Rust compiler.

The main features are

- Representation of fixed-point numbers up to 128 bits wide.
- Conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Comparisons between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Parsing from strings in decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Display as decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Arithmetic and logic operations.

This crate does *not* provide general analytic functions.

- No algebraic functions are provided, for example no `sqrt`or`pow`.
- No trigonometric functions are provided, for example no `sin`or`cos`.
- No other transcendental functions are provided, for example no
`log`or`exp`.

These functions are not provided because different implementations can have different trade-offs, for example trading some correctness for speed. Implementations can be provided in other crates.

- The *fixed-sqrt*crate

The conversions supported cover the following cases.

- Infallible lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using `From``Into`
- Infallible lossy conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric
primitives are provided using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`[their checked versions](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.checked_from_num).
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

## Quick examples

```
use I20F12;
// 19/3 = 6 1/3
let six_and_third = I20F12from_num / 3;
// four decimal digits for 12 binary digits
assert_eq!;
// find the ceil and convert to i32
assert_eq!;
// we can also compare directly to integers
assert_eq!;
```
The type [ I20F12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/type.I20F12.html) is a 32-bit fixed-point signed number with 20
integer bits and 12 fractional bits. It is an alias to

[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html)<

[U12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/extra/type.U12.html)>. The unsigned counterpart would be

[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````
use ;
// −8 ≤ I4F4 < 8 with steps of 1/16 (~0.06)
let a = I4F4from_num;
// multiplication and division by integers are possible
let ans1 = a / 5 * 17;
// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (~3.2)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (~0.0002)
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_num;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (~3.4)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (~3.2). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (~3.4).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.5/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

`from_num`## Using the *fixed* crate

The *fixed* crate is available on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fixed). To use
it in your crate, add it as a dependency inside [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "0.5.5"
```
The *fixed* crate requires rustc version 1.39.0 or later.

## Optional features

The *fixed* crate has four optional feature:

- `az`, disabled by default. This implements the cast traits provided by the- *az*crate
- `f16`, disabled by default. This provides conversion to/from- `f16`- `bf16`- *half*crate
- `serde`, disabled by default. This provides serialization support for the fixed-point types. This feature requires the- *serde*crate
- `std`, disabled by default. This is for features that are not possible under- `no_std`: currently the implementation of the- `Error`- `ParseFixedError`

To enable features, you can add the dependency like this to
[ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers.

- `FixedI8`- `FixedU8`
- `FixedI16`- `FixedU16`
- `FixedI32`- `FixedU32`
- `FixedI64`- `FixedU64`
- `FixedI128`- `FixedU128`

These types can have `Frac` fractional bits, where
0 ≤ `Frac` ≤ n and n is the total number of bits. When
`Frac` = 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an n-bit
integer. When `Frac` = n, the value x lies in the range
−0.5 ≤ x < 0.5 for signed numbers, and in the range
0 ≤ x < 1 for unsigned numbers.

Currently the [ typenum crate](https://crates.io/crates/typenum) is used for the fractional bit count

`Frac`; it is planned to move to [const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are supported by the Rust compiler.

The main features are

- Representation of fixed-point numbers up to 128 bits wide.
- Conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Comparisons between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Parsing from strings in decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Display as decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Arithmetic and logic operations.

This crate does *not* provide general analytic functions.

- No algebraic functions are provided, for example no `sqrt`or`pow`.
- No trigonometric functions are provided, for example no `sin`or`cos`.
- No other transcendental functions are provided, for example no
`log`or`exp`.

The conversions supported cover the following cases.

- Infallible lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using `From``Into`
- Infallible lossy conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric
primitives are provided using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`[their checked versions](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.5.1/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.checked_from_num).
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

# fixed 0.4.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/0.4.5

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers.

- `FixedI8`- `FixedU8`
- `FixedI16`- `FixedU16`
- `FixedI32`- `FixedU32`
- `FixedI64`- `FixedU64`
- `FixedI128`- `FixedU128`

These types can have `Frac` fractional bits, where
0 ≤ `Frac` ≤ n and n is the total number of bits. When
`Frac` = 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an n-bit
integer. When `Frac` = n, the value x lies in the range
−0.5 ≤ x < 0.5 for signed numbers, and in the range
0 ≤ x < 1 for unsigned numbers.

Currently the [ typenum crate](https://crates.io/crates/typenum) is used for the fractional bit count

`Frac`; it is planned to move to [const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are supported by the Rust compiler.

The main features are

- Representation of fixed-point numbers up to 128 bits wide.
- Conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Comparisons between fixed-point numbers and numeric primitives.
- Parsing from strings in decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Display as decimal, binary, octal and hexadecimal.
- Arithmetic and logic operations.

This crate does *not* provide general analytic functions.

- No algebraic functions are provided, for example no `sqrt`or`pow`.
- No trigonometric functions are provided, for example no `sin`or`cos`.
- No other transcendental functions are provided, for example no
`log`or`exp`.

The conversions supported cover the following cases.

- Infallible lossless conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using `From``Into`
- Infallible lossy conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are provided using the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked conversions between fixed-point numbers and numeric
primitives are provided using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`[their checked versions](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.checked_from_num).
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

## What’s new

### Version 0.4.5 news (2019-08-30)

- Bug fix: display of many decimal numbers was panicking in debug mode or including a leading zero in release mode.
- Many methods were added to `Wrapping`

### Version 0.4.4 news (2019-08-24)

- Bug fix: rounding could produce bad output for `Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`
- The following methods are now `const`functions:`is_power_of_two``abs``wrapping_abs``overflowing_abs`
- The method `round_to_zero`
- The method `round_ties_to_even`

### Version 0.4.3 news (2019-08-20)

- The *fixed*crate
- The precision argument is no longer ignored when formatting fixed-point numbers; precision should now be handled the same as for primitive floating-point numbers in the standard library.
- Parsing strings now rounds to the nearest with ties rounded to even.
- Checked versions of string parsing methods are now available as
inherent methods to all fixed-point numbers, and as methods in the
`Fixed`
- `Wrapping`- `FromStr`
- The following methods are now `const`functions:- `min_value`- `max_value`- `from_bits`- `to_bits`
- `count_ones`- `count_zeros`- `leading_zeros`- `trailing_zeros`- `rotate_left`- `rotate_right`
- `wrapping_neg`- `wrapping_add`- `wrapping_sub`- `wrapping_mul_int`- `wrapping_shl`- `wrapping_shr`
- `overflowing_neg`- `overflowing_add`- `overflowing_sub`- `overflowing_mul_int`- `overflowing_shl`- `overflowing_shr`
- `is_positive`- `is_negative`

- The associated constants `INT_NBITS``FRAC_NBITS`
- The reexports in the `frac`module and the`LeEqU*`traits were moved into the new`types::extra`

## Quick examples

```
use I20F12;
// 19/3 = 6 1/3
let six_and_third = I20F12from_num / 3;
// four decimal digits for 12 binary digits
assert_eq!;
// find the ceil and convert to i32
assert_eq!;
// we can also compare directly to integers
assert_eq!;
```
The type [ I20F12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/type.I20F12.html) is a 32-bit fixed-point signed number with 20
integer bits and 12 fractional bits. It is an alias to

[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html)<

[U12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/extra/type.U12.html)>. The unsigned counterpart would be

[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````
use ;
// −8 ≤ I4F4 < 8 with steps of 1/16 (~0.06)
let a = I4F4from_num;
// multiplication and division by integers are possible
let ans1 = a / 5 * 17;
// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (~3.2)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (~0.0002)
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_num;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (~3.4)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (~3.2). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (~3.4).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.5/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

`from_num`## Using the *fixed* crate

The *fixed* crate is available on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fixed). To use
it in your crate, add it as a dependency inside [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```

# fixed 0.4.3 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/0.4.3

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers. Currently it uses
the

[for the fractional bit count; it is planned to move to](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate[const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are implemented by the Rust compiler.

The crate provides the following types:

- `FixedI8`
- `FixedI16`
- `FixedI32`
- `FixedI64`
- `FixedI128`
- `FixedU8`
- `FixedU16`
- `FixedU32`
- `FixedU64`
- `FixedU128`

All fixed-point numbers can have `Frac` fractional bits, where `Frac`
can have any value from 0 up to and including the size of the number
in bits. When `Frac` is 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an
integer. When `Frac` is equal to the number of bits, the value of the
fixed-point number lies in the range −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5 for signed
fixed-point numbers, and in the range 0 ≤ *x* < 1 for unsigned
fixed-point numbers.

Various conversion methods are available:

- All lossless infallible conversions between fixed-point numbers
and numeric primitives are implemented. You can use `From``Into`
- For lossy infallible conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives, where the source type may have more fractional
bits than the destination type, the `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked conversions are provided between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives using the `FromFixed``ToFixed``from_num``to_num`
- Fixed-point numbers can be parsed from decimal strings using
`FromStr``from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`
- Fixed-point numbers can be converted to strings using `Display``Binary``Octal``LowerHex``UpperHex`

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.3/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html#method.from_num)

# fixed 0.4.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/0.4.2

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers. Currently it uses
the

[for the fractional bit count; it is planned to move to](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate[const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are implemented by the Rust compiler.

The crate provides the following types:

- `FixedI8`
- `FixedI16`
- `FixedI32`
- `FixedI64`
- `FixedI128`
- `FixedU8`
- `FixedU16`
- `FixedU32`
- `FixedU64`
- `FixedU128`

All fixed-point numbers can have `Frac` fractional bits, where `Frac`
can have any value from 0 up to and including the size of the number
in bits. When `Frac` is 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an
integer. When `Frac` is equal to the number of bits, the value of the
fixed-point number lies in the range −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5 for signed
fixed-point numbers, and in the range 0 ≤ *x* < 1 for unsigned
fixed-point numbers.

Various conversion methods are available:

- All lossless infallible conversions between fixed-point numbers
and numeric primitives are implemented. That is, you can use
`From``Into`
- For infallible conversions that are not lossless because the
source type may have more fractional bits than the destination
type, `LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- Checked conversions are provided between all types using the
`FromFixed``ToFixed`

## What’s new

### Version 0.4.2 news (2019-08-16)

- The new methods `from_num``to_num`
- The methods `from_fixed`,`to_fixed`,`from_int`,`to_int`,`from_float`, and`to_float`, and their checked versions, were deprecated.
- The new method `from_num``Wrapping`
- Bug fix: parsing of decimal fractions was fixed to give correctly rounded results for long decimal fraction strings, for example with four fractional bits, 0.96874999… (just below 31⁄32) and 0.96875 (31⁄32) are now parsed correctly as 0.9375 (15⁄16) and 1.0.

### Version 0.4.1 news (2019-08-12)

- All fixed-point types now implement `FromStr`
- The methods `from_str_binary``from_str_octal``from_str_hex`

### Version 0.4.0 news (2019-08-08)

- The *fixed*crate
- The `traits``Fixed``FixedSigned``FixedUnsigned``FromFixed``ToFixed``LossyFrom``LossyInto`
- The `saturating_neg``saturating_abs`
- The `consts`
- The `signum`

#### Incompatible changes

- The sealed traits `Int``Float``FromFixed``ToFixed`
- Deprecated methods were removed.

#### Contributors

### Other releases

Details on other releases can be found in [ RELEASES.md](https://gitlab.com/tspiteri/fixed/blob/master/RELEASES.md).

## Quick examples

```
// 20 integer bits, 12 fractional bits
use I20F12;
// 19/3 = 6 1/3
let six_and_third = I20F12from_int / 3;
// four decimal digits for 12 binary digits
assert_eq!;
// find the ceil and convert to i32
assert_eq!;
// we can also compare directly to integers
assert_eq!;
```
The type [ I20F12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/types/type.I20F12.html) is a 32-bit fixed-point signed number with 20
integer bits and 12 fractional bits. It is an alias to

[FixedI32](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html)<

[frac::U12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/frac/type.U12.html)>. The unsigned counterpart would be

[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````
// −8 ≤ I4F4 < 8 with steps of 1/16 (about 0.06)
use I4F4;
let a = I4F4from_int;
// multiplication and division by integers is possible
let ans1 = a / 5 * 17;
// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (3.19)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (about 0.0002)
use I4F12;
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_fixed;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (3.38)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (3.19). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (3.38).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.4.2/fixed/struct.FixedI8.html#method.from_fixed)

`from_fixed`## Using the *fixed* crate

The *fixed* crate is available on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fixed). To use
it in your crate, add it as a dependency inside [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]

```
If you are using the 2015 Rust edition, you also need to declare it by
adding this to your crate root (usually *lib.rs* or *main.rs*):

```

```
The *fixed* crate requires rustc version 1.31.0 or later.

## Optional features

The *fixed* crate has two optional feature:

- `f16`, disabled by default. This provides conversion to/from- `f16`- *half*crate
- `serde`, disabled by default. This provides serialization support for the fixed-point types. This feature requires the- *serde*crate

// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (3.19)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (about 0.0002)
use I4F12;
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_fixed;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (3.38)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (3.19). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (3.38).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.3/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.3/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.3/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.3/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.3/fixed/struct.FixedI8.html#method.from_fixed)

`from_fixed`## Using the *fixed* crate

The *fixed* crate is available on [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/fixed). To use
it in your crate, add it as a dependency inside [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "0.3.3"
```
If you are using the 2015 Rust edition, you also need to declare it by
adding this to your crate root (usually *lib.rs* or *main.rs*):

```
extern crate fixed;
```
The *fixed* crate requires rustc version 1.28.0 or later.

## Optional features

The *fixed* crate has two optional feature:

- `f16`, disabled by default. This provides conversion to/from- `f16`- *half*crate
- `serde`, disabled by default. This provides serialization support for the fixed-point types. This feature requires the- *serde*crate

To enable features, you can add the dependency like this to
[ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/dependencies.html):

```
[]
 = "0.3.3"
 = ["f16", "serde"]
```

# fixed 0.3.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/0.3.2

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers. Currently it uses
the

[for the fractional bit count; it is planned to move to](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate[const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are implemented by the Rust compiler.

The crate provides the following types:

- `FixedI8`
- `FixedI16`
- `FixedI32`
- `FixedI64`
- `FixedI128`
- `FixedU8`
- `FixedU16`
- `FixedU32`
- `FixedU64`
- `FixedU128`

All fixed-point numbers can have `Frac` fractional bits, where `Frac`
can have any value from 0 up to and including the size of the number
in bits. When `Frac` is 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an
integer. When `Frac` is equal to the number of bits, the value of the
fixed-point number lies in the range −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5 for signed
fixed-point numbers, and in the range 0 ≤ *x* < 1 for unsigned
fixed-point numbers.

All lossless infallible conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are implemented. That is, you can use [ From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html) or

[for the conversions that always work without losing any bits.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into`## What’s new

### Version 0.3.2 news (2019-02-27)

- The `Wrapping`

### Version 0.3.1 news (2019-02-07)

- Reimplement `From<bool>`

### Version 0.3.0 news (2019-02-03)

#### Highlights

- Every fixed-point type now supports conversion to/from all primitive number types, including checked versions of the conversions.
- Every fixed-point type now supports comparisons with all primitive number types.

### Other releases

## Quick examples

```

// 19/3 = 6 1/3
let six_and_third = I20F12from_int / 3;
// four decimal digits for 12 binary digits
assert_eq!;
// find the ceil and convert to i32
assert_eq!;
// we can also compare directly to integers
assert_eq!;
```
The type [ I20F12](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/types/type.I20F12.html) is a 32-bit fixed-point signed number with 20
integer bits and 12 fractional bits. It is an alias to

[. The unsigned counterpart would be](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/struct.FixedI32.html)

`FixedI32<frac::U12>`[. Aliases are provided for all combinations of integer and fractional bits adding up to a total of eight, 16, 32, 64 or 128 bits.](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/types/type.U20F12.html)

`U20F12````
// −8 ≤ I4F4 < 8 with steps of 1/16 (about 0.06)
use I4F4;
let a = I4F4from_int;
// multiplication and division by integers is possible
let ans1 = a / 5 * 17;
// 1 / 5 × 17 = 3 2/5 (3.4), but we get 3 3/16 (3.19)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// −8 ≤ I4F12 < 8 with steps of 1/4096 (about 0.0002)
use I4F12;
let wider_a = I4F12from;
let wider_ans = wider_a / 5 * 17;
let ans2 = I4F4from_fixed;
// now the answer is the much closer 3 6/16 (3.38)
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
The second example shows some precision and conversion issues. The low
precision of `a` means that `a / 5` is 3⁄16 instead of 1⁄5, leading to
an inaccurate result `ans1` = 3 3⁄16 (3.19). With a higher precision,
we get `wider_a / 5` equal to 819⁄4096, leading to a more accurate
intermediate result `wider_ans` = 3 1635⁄4096. When we convert back to
four fractional bits, we get `ans2` = 3 6⁄16 (3.38).

Note that we can convert from [ I4F4](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html) to

[using](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[, as the target type has the same number of integer bits and a larger number of fractional bits. Converting from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[to](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/types/type.I4F12.html)

`I4F12`[cannot use](https://docs.rs/fixed/0.3.2/fixed/types/type.I4F4.html)

`I4F4`[as we have less fractional bits, so we use](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html)

`From`[instead.](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedI8.html#method.from_fixed)

# fixed 0.1.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fixed/0.1.6

# Fixed-point numbers

The [ fixed crate](https://crates.io/crates/fixed) provides fixed-point numbers. Currently it uses
the

[for the fractional bit count; it is planned to move to](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate[const generics](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/44580)when they are implemented by the Rust compiler.

The crate provides the following types:

- `FixedI8`
- `FixedI16`
- `FixedI32`
- `FixedI64`
- `FixedI128`
- `FixedU8`
- `FixedU16`
- `FixedU32`
- `FixedU64`
- `FixedU128`

All fixed-point numbers can have `Frac` fractional bits, where `Frac`
can have any value from 0 up to and including the size of the number
in bits. When `Frac` is 0, the fixed-point number behaves like an
integer. When `Frac` is equal to the number of bits, the value of the
fixed-point number lies in the range −0.5 ≤ *x* < 0.5 for signed
fixed-point numbers, and in the range 0 ≤ *x* < 1 for unsigned
fixed-point numbers.

All lossless infallible conversions between fixed-point numbers and
numeric primitives are implemented. That is, you can use [ From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.From.html) or

[for the conversions that always work without losing any bits.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/convert/trait.Into.html)

`Into`## What’s new

# FixedU8 in fixed - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fixed/~1.31/fixed/struct.FixedU8.html

`pub struct FixedU8<Frac> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

An eight-bit unsigned number with `Frac` fractional bits.

The number has 8 bits, of which *f* = `Frac` are
fractional bits and 8 − *f* are integer bits.
The value *x* can lie in the range 0 ≤ *x* < 28/2 f. The difference between successive
numbers is constant throughout the range:

*Δ*= 1/2

.

*f*For `FixedU8<`, [U0](https://docs.rs/types/extra/type.U0.html)>*f* = 0 and
*Δ* = 1, and the fixed-point number behaves like a [ u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html) with the value lying in the range 0 ≤

*x*< 2

8. For

`FixedU8<`[U8](https://docs.rs/types/extra/type.U8.html)>,
*f*= 8 and

*Δ*= 1/2

8, and the value lies in the range 0 ≤

*x*< 1.

`Frac` is an [ Unsigned](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.Unsigned.html) as provided by the

[.](https://crates.io/crates/typenum)

*typenum*crate`FixedU8<Frac>` has the same size, alignment and ABI as
[ u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html); it is

`#[repr(transparent)]` with
[as the only non-zero-sized field.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)

`u8`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U3;
use fixed::FixedU8;
let eleven = FixedU8::<U3>::from_num(11);
assert_eq!(eleven, FixedU8::<U3>::from_bits(11 << 3));
assert_eq!(eleven, 11);
assert_eq!(eleven.to_string(), "11");
let two_point_75 = eleven / 4;
assert_eq!(two_point_75, FixedU8::<U3>::from_bits(11 << 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_75, 2.75);
assert_eq!(two_point_75.to_string(), "2.8");
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedU8%3CFrac%3E)### impl<Frac> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

The implementation of items in this block is independent
of the number of fractional bits `Frac`.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedU8%3CFrac%3E)

### impl<Frac> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

The implementation of items in this block is independent
of the number of fractional bits `Frac`.

The difference between any two successive representable numbers, *Δ*.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits, then
*Δ* = 1/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::DELTA, Fix::from_bits(1));
// binary 0.0001 is decimal 0.0625
assert_eq!(Fix::DELTA, 0.0625);
```
The smallest value that can be represented.

The minimum of unsigned numbers is 0.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MIN, Fix::from_bits(u8::MIN));
```
The largest value that can be represented.

If the number has *f* = `Frac` fractional bits, then the maximum is
(28 − 1)/2 f.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX, Fix::from_bits(u8::MAX));
```
Creates a fixed-point number that has a bitwise representation identical to the given integer.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 0010.0000 = 2
assert_eq!(Fix::from_bits(0b10_0000), 2);
```
Creates an integer that has a bitwise representation identical to the given fixed-point number.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 2 is 0010.0000
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).to_bits(), 0b10_0000);
```
Converts a fixed-point number from big endian to the target’s endianness.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
let f = Fix::from_bits(0x12);
if cfg!(target_endian = "big") {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_be(f), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_be(f), f.swap_bytes());
}
```
Converts a fixed-point number from little endian to the target’s endianness.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
let f = Fix::from_bits(0x12);
if cfg!(target_endian = "little") {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_le(f), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(Fix::from_le(f), f.swap_bytes());
}
```
Converts `self` to big endian from the target’s endianness.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;

if cfg!(target_endian = "big") {
    assert_eq!(f.to_be(), f);
} else {
    assert_eq!(f.to_be(), f.swap_bytes());
}
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

Multiplies two fixed-point numbers and returns a wider type to retain all precision.

If `self` has *f* fractional bits and 8 − *f*
integer bits, and `rhs` has *g* fractional bits and 8 − *g* integer bits, then the returned fixed-point number will
have *f* + *g* fractional bits and 16 − *f* − *g* integer bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-32)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U2, U4};
use fixed::FixedU8;
// decimal: 1.25 × 1.0625 = 1.328_125
// binary: 1.01 × 1.0001 = 1.010101
let a = FixedU8::<U2>::from_num(1.25);
let b = FixedU8::<U4>::from_num(1.0625);
assert_eq!(a.wide_mul(b), 1.328_125);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

Divides two fixed-point numbers and returns a wider type to retain more precision.

If `self` has *f* fractional bits
and 8 − *f* integer bits, and `rhs` has
*g* fractional bits and 8 − *g* integer
bits, then the returned fixed-point number will
have 8 + *f* − *g* fractional
bits and 8 − *f* + *g* integer
bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if the divisor is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-34)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U3, U5, U6};
use fixed::{FixedU8, FixedU16};
// decimal: 4.625 / 0.03125 = 148
// binary: 100.101 / 0.00001 = 10010100
let a = FixedU8::<U3>::from_num(4.625);
let b = FixedU8::<U5>::from_num(0.03125);
let ans: FixedU16<U6> = a.wide_div(b);
assert_eq!(ans, 148);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

Divides by a signed fixed-point number and returns a wider signed type to retain more precision.

integer bits, and `rhs` has *g* fractional bits and

integer bits, then the returned fixed-point number will have

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

Multiply and add. Returns `self` × `mul` + `add`.

The `mul` parameter can have a fixed-point type like
`self` but with a different number of fractional bits.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result
overflows. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value
can be returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the
future it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_mul_add](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#method.wrapping_mul_add)
instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(4).mul_add(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::from_num(3)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
```

Returns the distance from `self` to `other`.

The distance is the absolute value of the difference.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-40)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::ONE.dist(Fix::from_num(5)), Fix::from_num(4));
```
Returns the mean of `self` and `other`.

This method rounds the result down towards −∞. This is different from the
standard library [ midpoint](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html#method.midpoint), which rounds
towards 0. Rounding down preserves translation invariance, that is

`(a + t).mean(b + t)` = `a.mean(b) + t`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).mean(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(3.5));
```
Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 8
iterations for [ FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, this method panics if the result overflows.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be returned, but it
is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics; if wrapping is
required use [ wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#method.wrapping_hypot) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-42)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).hypot(Fix::from_num(4)), Fix::from_num(5));
```

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-6)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

When debug assertions are enabled, this method also panics if the result
overflows. When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future it panics;
if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#method.wrapping_inv_lerp) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-44)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
let start = Fix::from_num(2);
let end = Fix::from_num(3.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 0);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(2.75).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 0.5);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3.5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 1);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(5).inv_lerp::<U4>(start, end), 2);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)#### pub const fn [saturating_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

#### pub const fn [saturating_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.saturating_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, saturating on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 8
iterations for [ FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-77)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).saturating_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which does not fit
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).saturating_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    Fix::MAX
);
```

saturating on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-12)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)), Fix::MAX);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.saturating_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::from_num(0.5), Fix::ZERO), Fix::MIN);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)#### pub const fn [wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

#### pub const fn [wrapping_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, wrapping on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 8
iterations for [ FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-91)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).wrapping_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    Fix::from_num(5)
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which wraps to 1
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).wrapping_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    Fix::from_num(1)
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)#### pub const fn [wrapping_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_inv_lerp)<RetFrac: [LeEqU8](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU8.html)>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>,
    end: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<RetFrac>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

#### pub const fn [wrapping_inv_lerp](https://docs.rs#method.wrapping_inv_lerp)<RetFrac: [LeEqU8](https://docs.rs/types/extra/trait.LeEqU8.html)>(
    self,
    start: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>,
    end: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>,
) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<RetFrac>

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
wrapping on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Returns
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-15)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-93)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3).wrapping_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four), 0.5);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.wrapping_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2)
);
```

#### pub const fn [strict_hypot](https://docs.rs#method.strict_hypot)(self, other: [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>) -> [FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange, panicking on overflow.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 8
iterations for [ FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#panics-25)Panics

Panics if the result does not fit.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-108)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
```

Inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`,
panicking on overflow.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

Compute the hypotenuse of a right triange.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the hypotenuse and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), indicating whether an
overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The hypotenuse is equal to the square root of the sum of the squares of the operands.

This method uses an iterative method for its square root, with up to 8
iterations for [ FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html). The result is rounded down, and the
error is <

[. That is, result ≤ √(](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#associatedconstant.DELTA)

`DELTA``self`² + `other`²) < result + `DELTA`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-123)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// hypot(3, 4) == 5
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(4)),
    (Fix::from_num(5), false)
);
// hypot(8, 15) == 17, which wraps to 1
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(8).overflowing_hypot(Fix::from_num(15)),
    (Fix::from_num(1), true)
);

Overflowing next multiple of `other`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the next multiple and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating whether an

The next multiple is the smallest multiple of `other` that is ≥ `self`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-32)Panics

Panics if `other` is zero.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-124)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(4).overflowing_next_multiple_of(Fix::from_num(1.5)),
    (Fix::from_num(4.5), false)
);

    Fix::MAX.overflowing_next_multiple_of(max_minus_delta),
    (max_minus_delta.wrapping_mul_int(2), true)
);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

Overflowing inverse linear interpolation between `start` and `end`.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the result and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicationg whether an overflow
has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The computed value can have a fixed-point type like `self` but with a different
number of fractional bits.

Computes
(`self` − `start`) / (`end` − `start`).
This is 0 when `self` = `start`, and 1 when `self` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-33)Panics

Panics when `start` = `end`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-125)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
let two = Fix::from_num(2);
let four = Fix::from_num(4);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::from_num(3).overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(two, four),
    (Fix::from_num(0.5), false)
);
assert_eq!(
    Fix::MAX.overflowing_inv_lerp::<U4>(Fix::ZERO, Fix::from_num(0.5)),
    (Fix::MAX.wrapping_mul_int(2), true)
);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-FixedU8%3CFrac%3E-1)

The implementation of items in this block depends on the
number of fractional bits `Frac`.

Creates a fixed-point number from another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other number `src`for which`ToFixed``src.`.[to_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html#tymethod.to_fixed)()

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-50)Panics

For floating-point numbers, panics if the value is not [finite](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html#method.is_finite).

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_from_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#method.wrapping_from_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-130)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i32), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(3i64), Fix::from_bits(3 << 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f32), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
assert_eq!(Fix::from_num(1.75f64), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4-2)));
```
Converts a fixed-point number to another number.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other type `Dst`for which`FromFixed``Dst::`.[from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.from_fixed)(self)

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-51)Panics

When debug assertions are enabled, panics if the value does not fit.
When debug assertions are not enabled, the wrapped value can be
returned, but it is not considered a breaking change if in the future
it panics; if wrapping is required use [ wrapping_to_num](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html#method.wrapping_to_num) instead.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-131)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::U4;
use fixed::types::I30F2;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(src.to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b111));
// src >> 2 is 0.0111, which for I30F2 is truncated to 0.01
assert_eq!((src >> 2u32).to_num::<I30F2>(), I30F2::from_bits(0b1));
// 2.5 is 10.1 in binary
let two_point_5 = Fix::from_bits(0b101 << (4 - 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i32>(), 2);
assert_eq!(two_point_5.to_num::<i64>(), 2);
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f32>(), 1.625f32);
assert_eq!(one_point_625.to_num::<f64>(), 1.625f64);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)#### pub fn [checked_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.checked_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

#### pub fn [checked_from_num](https://docs.rs#method.checked_from_num)<Src: [ToFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.ToFixed.html)>(src: Src) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[FixedU8](https://docs.rs/struct.FixedU8.html)<Frac>>

Creates a fixed-point number from another number if it
fits, otherwise returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None).

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-136)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(src), Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2)));
// integer 0b1101 << (8 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let too_large = FixedU8::<U0>::from_bits(0b1101 << (8 - 7));
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (8 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(too_large), wrapped);
// integer 0b1101 << (8 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let large: u8 = 0b1101 << (8 - 7);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (8 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(1.75f32), expected);
// 1.75 << (8 - 4) wraps to binary 11000...
let large = 1.75 * 2f32.powi(8 - 4);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1100 << (8 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::wrapping_from_num(large), wrapped);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-140)Examples

```

use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::overflowing_from_num(src), (expected, false));
// integer 0b1101 << (8 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let too_large = FixedU8::<U0>::from_bits(0b1101 << (8 - 7));
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (8 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::overflowing_from_num(too_large), (wrapped, true));
assert_eq!(Fix::overflowing_from_num(3), (Fix::from_bits(3 << 4), false));
// integer 0b1101 << (8 - 7) will wrap to fixed-point 1010...
let large: u8 = 0b1101 << (8 - 7);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1010 << (8 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::overflowing_from_num(large), (wrapped, true));
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let expected = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
assert_eq!(Fix::overflowing_from_num(1.75f32), (expected, false));
// 1.75 << (8 - 4) wraps to binary 11000...
let large = 1.75 * 2f32.powi(8 - 4);
let wrapped = Fix::from_bits(0b1100 << (8 - 4));
assert_eq!(Fix::overflowing_from_num(large), (wrapped, true));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)#### pub fn [overflowing_to_num](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_to_num)<Dst: [FromFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html)>(self) -> (Dst, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/fixed/lib.rs.html#679-695)

#### pub fn [overflowing_to_num](https://docs.rs#method.overflowing_to_num)<Dst: [FromFixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html)>(self) -> (Dst, [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html))

Converts a fixed-point number to another number.

Returns a [tuple](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.tuple.html) of the number and a [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) indicating whether an
overflow has occurred. On overflow, the wrapped value is returned.

The other number can be:

- Another fixed-point number. Any extra fractional bits are discarded, which rounds towards −∞.
- An integer of type `i8``i16``i32``i64``i128``isize``u8``u16``u32``u64``u128``usize`
- A floating-point number of type [half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[f16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/binary16/struct.f16.html)[half](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/index.html)::[bf16](https://docs.rs/half/2.7.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/half/bfloat/struct.bf16.html)`f32``f64``F128`
- Any other type `Dst`for which`FromFixed``Dst::`.[overflowing_from_fixed](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.FromFixed.html#tymethod.overflowing_from_fixed)(self)

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-141)Examples

```
use fixed::types::extra::{U0, U4, U6};
use fixed::types::I16F16;
use fixed::FixedU8;
type Fix = FixedU8<U4>;
// 1.75 is 1.11 in binary
let src = Fix::from_bits(0b111 << (4 - 2));
let expected = I16F16::from_bits(0b111 << (16 - 2));
assert_eq!(src.overflowing_to_num::<I16F16>(), (expected, false));
type TooFewIntBits = FixedU8<U6>;
let wrapped = TooFewIntBits::from_bits(Fix::MAX.to_bits() << 2);
assert_eq!(Fix::MAX.overflowing_to_num::<TooFewIntBits>(), (wrapped, true));
// 2.5 is 10.1 in binary
let two_point_5 = Fix::from_bits(0b101 << (4 - 1));
assert_eq!(two_point_5.overflowing_to_num::<i32>(), (2, false));
let does_not_fit = FixedU8::<U0>::MAX;
let wrapped = -1i8;
assert_eq!(does_not_fit.overflowing_to_num::<i8>(), (wrapped, true));
// 1.625 is 1.101 in binary
let one_point_625 = Fix::from_bits(0b1101 << (4 - 3));
assert_eq!(one_point_625.overflowing_to_num::<f32>(), (1.625f32, false));
```
